title: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) - MCQ Bank for BJSC Preparation
coverage: Sections 2-35 (definitions & interpretation nuances) and Orders I-IX in depth (parties, frame of suit, recognized agents/pleaders, institution, pleadings, plaint, written statement, summons, appearance & default)
note: Focus is on precise wording and commonly-tested exceptions/provisos, since BJSC MCQs often hinge on exact statutory language.

mcqs.question: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 came into force on:
mcqs.answer: 1 January 1909

mcqs.question: CPC 1908 extends to:
mcqs.answer: The whole of Bangladesh

mcqs.question: Under S.2, 'decree' does NOT include:
options: An order of dismissal for default
mcqs.answer: An order of dismissal for default

mcqs.question: A decree which fully disposes of the suit is called:
mcqs.answer: Final decree

mcqs.question: Under S.2(14), 'order' means:
options: The formal expression of any decision of a civil court which is not a decree
Any decision of a criminal court
mcqs.answer: The formal expression of any decision of a civil court which is not a decree

mcqs.question: 'Mesne profits' relate to profits which a person in wrongful possession:
options: Actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received, together with interest, but excluding profits due to his own improvements
mcqs.answer: Actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received, together with interest, but excluding profits due to his own improvements

mcqs.question: 'Decree-holder' means:
options: Any person in whose favour a decree has been passed or an order capable of execution has been made
mcqs.answer: Any person in whose favour a decree has been passed or an order capable of execution has been made

mcqs.question: S.9 CPC provides that courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature except:
options: Suits of which cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred
mcqs.answer: Suits of which cognizance is expressly or impliedly barred

mcqs.question: Under the Explanation to S.9, a suit in which the right to property or office is contested is a suit of a civil nature even though:
options: The right may depend entirely on the decision of questions as to religious rites or ceremonies
mcqs.answer: The right may depend entirely on the decision of questions as to religious rites or ceremonies

mcqs.question: S.11 (Res judicata) bars a court from trying an issue that has been:
options: Directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, litigating under the same title, in a competent court, and heard and finally decided
mcqs.answer: Directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, litigating under the same title, in a competent court, and heard and finally decided

mcqs.question: Explanation IV to S.11 embodies the principle of:
mcqs.answer: Constructive res judicata

mcqs.question: Res judicata applies to:
mcqs.answer: Both suits and execution proceedings

mcqs.question: Suits for recovery of immovable property must be instituted in the court within whose local limits the property is situate, under:
A suit against a defendant for compensation for wrong done to person or movable property may, at the plaintiff's option, be filed where:
options: The wrong was done or where the defendant resides/carries on business/works for gain
Only where the wrong was done
Only in the High Court Division
mcqs.answer: The wrong was done or where the defendant resides/carries on business/works for gain

mcqs.question: Objections as to the place of suing (territorial jurisdiction) must be raised:
options: At the earliest possible opportunity, and in cases where issues are settled, at or before such settlement
mcqs.answer: At the earliest possible opportunity, and in cases where issues are settled, at or before such settlement

mcqs.question: S.10 CPC deals with:
options: Stay of suit where the matter is directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties
mcqs.answer: Stay of suit where the matter is directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties

mcqs.question: S.13 lists grounds on which a foreign judgment is NOT conclusive; these include all EXCEPT:
options: Pronounced by a court of competent jurisdiction
Founded on an incorrect view of international law where recognised law of Bangladesh applies
Sustains a claim founded on a breach of local law
mcqs.answer: Pronounced by a court of competent jurisdiction

mcqs.question: Power to transfer suits, appeals or other proceedings from one court to another subordinate court is given by:
Under Order I Rule 1, all persons may be joined as plaintiffs in one suit if the right to relief arises out of the same act/transaction and there is a common question of:
mcqs.answer: Law or fact

mcqs.question: A necessary party is one:
options: Without whom no effective decree can be passed
Who has no interest in the suit
mcqs.answer: Without whom no effective decree can be passed

mcqs.question: Misjoinder or non-joinder of parties:
options: Shall not defeat a suit, and the court may deal with the matter as regards the parties actually before it
mcqs.answer: Shall not defeat a suit, and the court may deal with the matter as regards the parties actually before it

mcqs.question: Order I Rule 10 empowers the court to:
mcqs.answer: Add or strike out parties

mcqs.question: Order II Rule 2 provides that a plaintiff must include the whole of the claim to which he is entitled, failing which he:
options: Shall not afterwards sue for any part omitted or relinquished, without leave of the court
mcqs.answer: Shall not afterwards sue for any part omitted or relinquished, without leave of the court

mcqs.question: Joinder of causes of action by one plaintiff against one defendant is governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order II Rule 3

mcqs.question: A suit is instituted by the presentation of a:
options: Plaint to the court or such officer as it appoints
mcqs.answer: Plaint to the court or such officer as it appoints

mcqs.question: Particulars a plaint must contain under Order VII Rule 1 include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Evidence to be led at trial
Name, description and place of residence of plaintiff and defendant
Facts constituting the cause of action
mcqs.answer: Evidence to be led at trial

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 11 empowers the court to reject a plaint on grounds including:
options: Where it does not disclose a cause of action
Where the defendant fails to appear
mcqs.answer: Where it does not disclose a cause of action

mcqs.question: Rejection of a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 is deemed to be a:
mcqs.answer: Decree

mcqs.question: Return of plaint for presentation to the proper court is provided under:
mcqs.answer: Order VII Rule 10

mcqs.question: Under Order VIII Rule 1, the defendant must file the written statement of his defence within:
options: A period fixed by the court, subject to statutory time-limits
mcqs.answer: A period fixed by the court, subject to statutory time-limits

mcqs.question: A set-off is a claim by the defendant which is:
options: An ascertained sum of money legally recoverable by him from the plaintiff, pleaded as a cross-claim
mcqs.answer: An ascertained sum of money legally recoverable by him from the plaintiff, pleaded as a cross-claim

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 2 requires every pleading to contain a statement of material facts:
options: In a concise form, not the evidence by which the facts are to be proved
In exhaustive detail with all evidence
mcqs.answer: In a concise form, not the evidence by which the facts are to be proved

mcqs.question: Amendment of pleadings is dealt with under:
mcqs.answer: Order VI Rule 17

mcqs.question: Particulars of fraud, misrepresentation, breach of trust, wilful default or undue influence must be specifically stated under:
mcqs.answer: Order VI Rule 4

mcqs.question: Summons to a defendant is issued for the purpose of:
options: Requiring him to appear and answer the claim
Only informing him of the decree
mcqs.answer: Requiring him to appear and answer the claim

mcqs.question: Where the defendant cannot be found, service of summons may be made on:
options: Any adult male or female member of his family residing with him
No one; suit must be dismissed
mcqs.answer: Any adult male or female member of his family residing with him

mcqs.question: Substituted service (e.g., by affixing a copy on the outer door, or by publication) is permitted under:
mcqs.answer: Order V Rule 20

mcqs.question: Where neither party appears when a suit is called for hearing, the court may:
mcqs.answer: Dismiss the suit

mcqs.question: Where the plaintiff does not appear and the defendant does, the court may:
options: Dismiss the suit unless the defendant admits the claim, in which case it may pass a decree
mcqs.answer: Dismiss the suit unless the defendant admits the claim, in which case it may pass a decree

mcqs.question: Where the defendant does not appear and the plaintiff does, and summons is proved to be duly served, the court may:
mcqs.answer: Proceed ex-parte

mcqs.question: An application to set aside an ex-parte decree may be made by the defendant on satisfying the court that:
options: Summons was not duly served, or he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing
He wants a fresh trial without reason
mcqs.answer: Summons was not duly served, or he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing

mcqs.question: Order X deals with:
options: Oral examination of parties by the court
mcqs.answer: Oral examination of parties by the court

mcqs.question: Interrogatories may be delivered by one party to another with the leave of the court under:
mcqs.answer: Order XI Rule 1

mcqs.question: Notice to admit facts/documents is provided under:
mcqs.answer: Order XII Rules 4 and 8

mcqs.question: Where admissions of fact are made, the court may on application:
options: Give judgment or make an order on the basis of such admissions without waiting for full trial
mcqs.answer: Give judgment or make an order on the basis of such admissions without waiting for full trial

mcqs.question: Documentary evidence must ordinarily be produced at or before the:
mcqs.answer: Settlement of issues

mcqs.question: Issues are framed by the court from the allegations made in the pleadings, and materials placed before it, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XIV Rule 1

mcqs.question: Issues of fact and law are called:
mcqs.answer: Mixed issues

mcqs.question: Where issues both of law and fact arise, and the court is of opinion that the case may be disposed of on the issues of law alone, it may try those issues first; this is under:
mcqs.answer: Order XIV Rule 2

mcqs.question: Order XV deals with:
options: Disposal of the suit at the first hearing where parties are not at issue
mcqs.answer: Disposal of the suit at the first hearing where parties are not at issue

mcqs.question: Order XVI deals with:
mcqs.answer: Summoning and attendance of witnesses

mcqs.question: Order XVII empowers the court to grant time and adjourn the hearing of the suit, but generally costs occasioned by the adjournment shall be:
options: Paid by the party seeking it, as the court thinks fit
mcqs.answer: Paid by the party seeking it, as the court thinks fit

mcqs.question: Order XVIII deals with:
options: Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses
mcqs.answer: Hearing of the suit and examination of witnesses

mcqs.question: Under Order XVIII Rule 1, the party having the right to begin is normally:
options: The plaintiff, unless the defendant admits the facts and contends that the plaintiff is not entitled to relief on a point of law
mcqs.answer: The plaintiff, unless the defendant admits the facts and contends that the plaintiff is not entitled to relief on a point of law

mcqs.question: Order XIX deals with:
mcqs.answer: Affidavits

mcqs.question: Judgment means the statement given by the judge of the grounds of a decree or order, as defined in:
A judgment must be pronounced in open court, and once signed, alteration is generally not permitted except to correct:
options: Findings of fact on review basis only
mcqs.answer: Clerical or arithmetical mistakes

mcqs.question: Contents required in a decree under Order XX Rule 6 include the number of the suit, names/descriptions of parties, particulars of claim, and:
options: The relief granted or other determination of the suit
mcqs.answer: The relief granted or other determination of the suit

mcqs.question: A preliminary decree is passed when:
options: Further proceedings are required before the suit can be completely disposed of, e.g., in partition or accounts suits
The suit is dismissed for default
mcqs.answer: Further proceedings are required before the suit can be completely disposed of, e.g., in partition or accounts suits

mcqs.question: S.35 CPC gives the court discretion regarding:
options: Costs of and incident to all suits
Fixed statutory costs with no discretion
mcqs.answer: Costs of and incident to all suits

mcqs.question: Compensatory costs for false or vexatious claims or defences may be awarded under:
mcqs.answer: S.35A

mcqs.question: Costs for causing delay may be imposed on a party under:
mcqs.answer: S.35B

mcqs.question: S.34 CPC empowers the court to order interest:
options: On the principal sum adjudged, both pre-decree and post-decree (future interest)
No interest can ever be granted
Only if agreed by both parties
mcqs.answer: On the principal sum adjudged, both pre-decree and post-decree (future interest)

mcqs.question: The court which passed the decree, or to which it is sent for execution, is called the:
mcqs.answer: Executing court

mcqs.question: Under S.38, a decree may be executed either by the court which passed it or by the court to which it is:
mcqs.answer: Sent for execution

mcqs.question: Questions relating to execution, discharge or satisfaction of the decree, arising between the parties to the suit, shall be determined:
options: By the executing court and not by a separate suit
Only by filing a fresh suit
mcqs.answer: By the executing court and not by a separate suit

mcqs.question: Modes of execution under Order XXI include all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Arrest and detention in civil prison
mcqs.answer: Framing of issues

mcqs.question: Arrest and detention in civil prison in execution of a money decree is subject to restrictions, including exemption for:
mcqs.answer: Women, in most circumstances

mcqs.question: Property which cannot be attached in execution of a decree (e.g., necessary wearing apparel, tools of artisans, etc.) is listed under:
mcqs.answer: S.60 proviso

mcqs.question: A person whose immovable property is sold in execution may apply to set aside the sale on the ground of material irregularity or fraud in publishing/conducting the sale under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 90

mcqs.question: Resistance to delivery of possession by a judgment-debtor or third party is dealt with under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rules 97-103

mcqs.question: S.144 CPC deals with:
options: Restitution - placing parties in the position they would have occupied but for a decree/order later varied or reversed
mcqs.answer: Restitution - placing parties in the position they would have occupied but for a decree/order later varied or reversed

mcqs.question: S.75 empowers the court to issue a commission to:
options: Examine any person, make a local investigation, adjust accounts, or make a partition
Only record oral evidence of the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Examine any person, make a local investigation, adjust accounts, or make a partition

mcqs.question: Under S.79, a suit by or against the Government must be instituted in the name of:
options: The Government of Bangladesh, as the case may be
mcqs.answer: The Government of Bangladesh, as the case may be

mcqs.question: Prior notice before instituting a suit against the Government or a public officer in respect of an act purporting to be done in his official capacity is required under:
The minimum period of notice required under S.80 before filing suit against the Government is:
mcqs.answer: Two months

mcqs.question: S.88 and Order XXXV deal with:
options: Interpleader suits, where two or more persons claim adversely the same debt/property from a person not claiming interest therein
mcqs.answer: Interpleader suits, where two or more persons claim adversely the same debt/property from a person not claiming interest therein

mcqs.question: S.89A/89B/89C of the Bangladesh CPC (as amended) deal with:
options: Alternative dispute resolution - mediation and settlement conference
Arbitration under the old repealed provisions only
mcqs.answer: Alternative dispute resolution - mediation and settlement conference

mcqs.question: S.91 and S.92 deal respectively with:
mcqs.answer: Public nuisances and public charities/trusts

mcqs.question: S.94 empowers the court, for the purpose of preventing the ends of justice from being defeated, to order arrest, attachment before judgment, temporary injunction, appointment of a receiver, and other:
options: Interlocutory orders as may appear to it necessary
mcqs.answer: Interlocutory orders as may appear to it necessary

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII deals with:
mcqs.answer: Arrest and attachment before judgment

mcqs.question: Order XXXIX deals with:
options: Permanent injunctions under the Specific Relief Act only
mcqs.answer: Temporary injunctions and interlocutory orders

mcqs.question: For grant of a temporary injunction, the applicant must ordinarily establish:
options: A prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury
Only that the suit has been filed
Only that the defendant is wealthy
mcqs.answer: A prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury

mcqs.question: Order XL deals with the appointment of:
mcqs.answer: Receivers

mcqs.question: Appeals from original decrees are governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI

mcqs.question: An appeal shall be filed by presenting a memorandum of appeal, which must set forth grounds of objection, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 1

mcqs.question: Appeals from appellate decrees (second appeals) are governed by:
options: Order XLII, and lie only on grounds specified in S.100 (substantial question of law)
mcqs.answer: Order XLII, and lie only on grounds specified in S.100 (substantial question of law)

mcqs.question: S.100 CPC restricts second appeal to cases involving:
mcqs.answer: A substantial question of law

mcqs.question: Appeals from orders (as distinguished from decrees) are governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XLIII and S.104

mcqs.question: Appeals by indigent persons are governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XLIV

mcqs.question: S.113 CPC empowers a subordinate court to state a case and refer it for the opinion of the High Court Division; this is called:
mcqs.answer: Reference

mcqs.question: S.114 read with Order XLVII provides for:
options: Review of judgment by the same court that passed it, on discovery of new evidence, error apparent on face of record, or other sufficient reason
mcqs.answer: Review of judgment by the same court that passed it, on discovery of new evidence, error apparent on face of record, or other sufficient reason

mcqs.question: S.115 CPC empowers the High Court Division to call for the record of any case decided by a subordinate court where no appeal lies, if the subordinate court:
options: Appears to have exercised jurisdiction not vested in it by law, or failed to exercise jurisdiction vested, or acted illegally/with material irregularity
Simply reached a different conclusion of fact
mcqs.answer: Appears to have exercised jurisdiction not vested in it by law, or failed to exercise jurisdiction vested, or acted illegally/with material irregularity

mcqs.question: S.151 CPC saves the inherent power of the court to:
options: Make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court
Override any express provision of the Code
mcqs.answer: Make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court

mcqs.question: S.148 empowers the court to:
options: Enlarge time fixed or granted for doing any act prescribed or allowed by the Code
Extend limitation periods under the Limitation Act indefinitely
mcqs.answer: Enlarge time fixed or granted for doing any act prescribed or allowed by the Code

mcqs.question: S.152/S.153 deal with:
options: Amendment of judgments, decrees or orders for correcting clerical or arithmetical mistakes or errors arising from accidental slip
mcqs.answer: Amendment of judgments, decrees or orders for correcting clerical or arithmetical mistakes or errors arising from accidental slip

mcqs.question: Order XXXIII allows a person to sue without payment of requisite court fees if he is:
options: An indigent person, as defined therein
mcqs.answer: An indigent person, as defined therein

mcqs.question: Order XXXII deals with suits by or against:
options: Minors and persons of unsound mind
mcqs.answer: Minors and persons of unsound mind

mcqs.question: A suit on behalf of a minor must be instituted in his name by his:
options: Guardian ad litem always as plaintiff himself
mcqs.answer: Next friend

mcqs.question: Order XXX permits two or more persons claiming or being liable as partners to sue or be sued in the name of the:
options: Individual partners only, never the firm
mcqs.answer: Firm

mcqs.question: S.36 CPC provides that provisions relating to execution of decrees apply, so far as applicable, to the execution of:
options: Orders (including orders for payment of money)
mcqs.answer: Orders (including orders for payment of money)

mcqs.question: Under S.37, 'court which passed a decree' includes, where the decree has been passed in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction, the:
mcqs.answer: Court of first instance

mcqs.question: A decree may be transferred for execution to another court under S.39 on the application of the decree-holder, if, among other grounds, the judgment-debtor:
options: Actually and voluntarily resides, or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of that other court's jurisdiction
mcqs.answer: Actually and voluntarily resides, or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of that other court's jurisdiction

mcqs.question: S.42 provides that the court executing a decree sent to it has the same powers as if it had passed the decree itself, and is subject to the same:
mcqs.answer: Rules regarding execution of decrees

mcqs.question: Where a decree is transferred for execution, S.41 requires the court to which it is sent to certify to the court which passed it:
options: The fact of such execution, or the failure of execution and the reasons therefor
Only in case of full satisfaction
mcqs.answer: The fact of such execution, or the failure of execution and the reasons therefor

mcqs.question: S.50 provides that where a judgment-debtor dies before the decree has been fully satisfied, the decree-holder may apply to execute it against the:
options: Legal representative of the deceased, limited to the property of the deceased that has come into his hands
mcqs.answer: Legal representative of the deceased, limited to the property of the deceased that has come into his hands

mcqs.question: S.51 empowers the court, on the application of the decree-holder, to order execution of the decree by delivery of property, attachment and sale, arrest and detention, appointment of a receiver, or:
options: Such other manner as the nature of the relief granted may require
Only by sale of immovable property
mcqs.answer: Such other manner as the nature of the relief granted may require

mcqs.question: Before ordering arrest and detention of a judgment-debtor, the court must, except in certain cases, issue a notice under:
options: S.54 / Order XXI Rule 37, calling upon him to show cause why he should not be committed to civil prison
Only a warrant of arrest directly
mcqs.answer: S.54 / Order XXI Rule 37, calling upon him to show cause why he should not be committed to civil prison

mcqs.question: The maximum period for which a judgment-debtor may ordinarily be detained in civil prison in execution of a decree is:
mcqs.answer: Six months

mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor released from detention on the ground of the decree being satisfied cannot be re-arrested under the:
options: This is not addressed in the Code
mcqs.answer: Same decree

mcqs.question: S.60 lists property liable to attachment and sale in execution, and provides that certain property is NOT liable to attachment, such as:
options: Necessary wearing apparel, cooking vessels, and tools of artisans (subject to conditions)
mcqs.answer: Necessary wearing apparel, cooking vessels, and tools of artisans (subject to conditions)

mcqs.question: Attachment of movable property in the possession of the judgment-debtor is effected under Order XXI by:
options: Notice to the judgment-debtor's employer only
mcqs.answer: Actual seizure

mcqs.question: Attachment of immovable property is effected under Order XXI Rule 54 by an order prohibiting the judgment-debtor from:
options: Transferring or charging the property in any way
mcqs.answer: Transferring or charging the property in any way

mcqs.question: Attachment of a decree (i.e., a decree for payment of money or sale of property held by the judgment-debtor against a third person) is governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 53

mcqs.question: Attachment of salary or allowances of a government servant, in execution of a decree other than a decree for maintenance, is subject to a statutory:
options: Attachment only with the President's consent
mcqs.answer: Portion being exempt from attachment

mcqs.question: Where a person other than the judgment-debtor objects that property attached in execution is not liable to attachment because he holds an interest in it, he may make a claim or objection under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 58

mcqs.question: An order determining a claim or objection under Order XXI Rule 58 has the force of a decree, and the aggrieved party's remedy is to:
options: File a suit to establish the right claimed, within the period allowed by law, or appeal as if it were a decree
mcqs.answer: File a suit to establish the right claimed, within the period allowed by law, or appeal as if it were a decree

mcqs.question: Before the sale of any property in execution, the court must issue a proclamation of sale under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 66

mcqs.question: A proclamation of sale of immovable property must state, among other things, the property to be sold, its revenue if any, encumbrances, and the:
options: Amount for the recovery of which the sale is ordered
Names of all previous owners for 50 years
mcqs.answer: Amount for the recovery of which the sale is ordered

mcqs.question: No sale of immovable property in execution shall, without the consent in writing of the judgment-debtor, take place before the expiry of at least:
options: Fifteen days from the date of proclamation
mcqs.answer: Fifteen days from the date of proclamation

mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor may, at any time before the sale is concluded, apply to have the sale postponed on depositing the amount decreed together with:
mcqs.answer: Interest and costs of execution

mcqs.question: An application to set aside a sale of immovable property on the ground of material irregularity or fraud in publishing or conducting the sale, resulting in substantial injury, may be made under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 90

mcqs.question: An application by the judgment-debtor to set aside a sale on depositing the decretal amount is made under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 89

mcqs.question: The purchaser at a court sale may apply to have the sale set aside on the ground that the judgment-debtor had no saleable interest under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 91

mcqs.question: Where no application to set aside the sale is made, or such application is disallowed, the court shall make an order:
options: Confirming the sale, whereupon it becomes absolute
mcqs.answer: Confirming the sale, whereupon it becomes absolute

mcqs.question: Where the sold property is in the occupancy of the judgment-debtor or a person bound by the decree, delivery of possession to the purchaser is effected under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 95

mcqs.question: Where the holder of a decree for possession of immovable property is resisted or obstructed by any person in obtaining possession, he may make an application complaining of such resistance under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 97

mcqs.question: Where resistance to delivery of possession is occasioned by a person claiming an independent right (not merely as a transferee pendente lite), the court, under Order XXI Rule 101, must:
options: Adjudicate upon the claim to the right and title of the property
Refer the matter to a civil suit compulsorily in every case
mcqs.answer: Adjudicate upon the claim to the right and title of the property

mcqs.question: Where money is paid or property delivered to the decree-holder out of court in satisfaction of a decree, the decree-holder is required to certify such payment to the court, failing which the court may not recognise it under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 2

mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor may pay the decretal amount into court, and such payment is regulated under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 1

mcqs.question: S.73 CPC deals with rateable distribution of assets realised in execution among:
options: Decree-holders who have applied for execution against the same judgment-debtor before receipt of the assets
Only the first decree-holder to apply
mcqs.answer: Decree-holders who have applied for execution against the same judgment-debtor before receipt of the assets

mcqs.question: S.49 deals with execution of a decree against a firm and provides that it may be executed against the property of the firm and against any person who has appeared in his own name under Order XXX or:
options: Admitted on the pleadings to be a partner
A minor without a next friend
mcqs.answer: Admitted on the pleadings to be a partner

mcqs.question: S.46 empowers the court which passed a decree, upon the application of the decree-holder, to issue a precept to another court to attach property of the judgment-debtor, which shall remain in force for:
options: Two months, unless extended by the court which passed the decree
mcqs.answer: Two months, unless extended by the court which passed the decree

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rules 18-20 deal with:
options: Execution of cross-decrees and cross-claims, including set-off between them
mcqs.answer: Execution of cross-decrees and cross-claims, including set-off between them

mcqs.question: The court which passed a decree may, on sufficient cause being shown, stay execution of the decree under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 26

mcqs.question: Where a suit is pending in a court against the holder of a decree of another court, on the same subject-matter and between the same parties, the court may stay execution under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 29

mcqs.question: An appellate court's power to stay execution of a decree pending appeal is provided under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 5

mcqs.question: An application for execution of a decree is subject to the period of limitation prescribed under the Limitation Act, generally:
options: Twelve years from the date of the decree (subject to specific provisions)
mcqs.answer: Twelve years from the date of the decree (subject to specific provisions)
mcqs.reference: Limitation Act, read with S.48 (as historically applicable)

mcqs.question: Where a decree has been adjusted wholly or in part to the satisfaction of the decree-holder, the judgment-debtor may apply to the court which passed the decree to have such adjustment recorded under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 2

mcqs.question: Attachment of debts due to the judgment-debtor from a third person (garnishee) is governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 46

mcqs.question: S.96 CPC provides that an appeal shall lie from every decree passed by any court exercising original jurisdiction, subject to exceptions such as:
options: A decree passed with the consent of parties
Any ex-parte decree, which can never be appealed
Decrees below a certain value in all cases
mcqs.answer: A decree passed with the consent of parties

mcqs.question: S.96(4) bars appeals in cases where the subject matter of the original suit is cognizable by courts of small causes, and the amount does not exceed a specified value, except on a question of:
mcqs.answer: Law

mcqs.question: An appeal from an ex-parte decree lies under S.96, in addition to the remedy of applying to set aside the decree under:
mcqs.answer: Order IX Rule 13

mcqs.question: S.104 lists orders from which an appeal lies, such as an order under S.35A (compensatory costs), an order refusing to add or strike out a party, and orders under Order XXXIX (injunctions), among others, and expressly states that no appeal lies from any:
options: Other order except as provided in the body of the Code
Interlocutory order whatsoever, in all circumstances
mcqs.answer: Other order except as provided in the body of the Code

mcqs.question: S.100 permits second appeal to the High Court Division from a decree passed in appeal by a subordinate court, if the case involves a substantial question of law, and S.101 clarifies that no second appeal lies except on the ground:
mcqs.answer: Mentioned in S.100

mcqs.question: S.103 empowers the High Court Division, in second appeal, to determine an issue of fact necessary for disposal of the appeal, if the evidence on record is sufficient, provided such issue:
options: Has not been determined by the lower appellate court, or has been wrongly determined by reason of a decision on a substantial question of law
Involves a new cause of action
mcqs.answer: Has not been determined by the lower appellate court, or has been wrongly determined by reason of a decision on a substantial question of law

mcqs.question: A respondent, though he may not have appealed from any part of the decree, may, upon being served with notice of appeal, file cross-objections under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 22

mcqs.question: Production of additional evidence in the appellate court is generally not allowed except in circumstances specified under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 27

mcqs.question: An appellate court may dismiss an appeal summarily without sending notice to the lower court or issuing notice to the respondent, after hearing the appellant, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 11

mcqs.question: Where the lower court disposes of the suit on a preliminary point without recording findings on other issues, and the appellate court reverses the decree, it may remand the case under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 23

mcqs.question: Order XLI Rule 33 empowers the appellate court to pass any decree or order which ought to have been passed, and may do so:
options: In favour of all or any of the respondents or parties, although they may not have filed an appeal or objection
Only in favour of the appellant
Never in favour of a non-appealing party
mcqs.answer: In favour of all or any of the respondents or parties, although they may not have filed an appeal or objection

mcqs.question: S.109 CPC deals with appeals to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court from decrees or final orders of the High Court Division, subject to:
options: Conditions and the Constitution/relevant law regulating such appeals
A separate statute unrelated to the CPC entirely
mcqs.answer: Conditions and the Constitution/relevant law regulating such appeals

mcqs.question: Limitation for filing a first appeal from a decree is generally governed by the Limitation Act and is commonly:
options: Ninety days from the date of the decree (subject to specific provisions)
mcqs.answer: Ninety days from the date of the decree (subject to specific provisions)

mcqs.question: S.113 read with Order XLVI permits a subordinate court to refer a question of law to the High Court Division where it entertains reasonable doubt as to a question of law and the case is one in which:
options: No appeal lies from the decree or order
The suit has been dismissed for default
mcqs.answer: No appeal lies from the decree or order

mcqs.question: A subordinate court may also refer to the High Court Division a question as to the validity of an Act, Ordinance or Regulation under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLVI Rule 1

mcqs.question: Grounds for review under Order XLVII Rule 1 include discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within the applicant's knowledge, mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or:
options: A change in the composition of the bench
New arguments not raised earlier without justification
mcqs.answer: Any other sufficient reason

mcqs.question: An application for review must ordinarily be made to:
options: The same judge/court that passed the decree or order
mcqs.answer: The same judge/court that passed the decree or order

mcqs.question: Where a review is sought on the ground that the decree/order was passed without the applicant's knowledge or that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing, the applicant must satisfy the court in a manner similar to:
options: An application to set aside an ex-parte decree under Order IX Rule 13
An application for attachment before judgment
mcqs.answer: An application to set aside an ex-parte decree under Order IX Rule 13

mcqs.question: Under S.115, the High Court Division's revisional jurisdiction can be exercised only where no appeal lies to the High Court Division from the order/decree, and where the subordinate court's error goes to:
options: Jurisdiction or illegality/material irregularity in exercise of jurisdiction
mcqs.answer: Jurisdiction or illegality/material irregularity in exercise of jurisdiction

mcqs.question: Unlike an appeal, a revision does not ordinarily allow the revisional court to:
options: Re-appreciate evidence and substitute its own findings of fact for those of the trial court
Examine material irregularity in exercise of jurisdiction
mcqs.answer: Re-appreciate evidence and substitute its own findings of fact for those of the trial court

mcqs.question: S.63 provides that where property is under attachment by orders of two or more courts, the property shall be dealt with as under attachment by the court of:
options: The highest grade, or, where the courts are of the same grade, by the court whose attachment is subsisting
Whichever attached first, regardless of grade
mcqs.answer: The highest grade, or, where the courts are of the same grade, by the court whose attachment is subsisting

mcqs.question: S.64 provides that any private transfer or delivery of property attached in execution, or of any interest therein, made contrary to such attachment, is:
options: Void as against claims enforceable under the attachment
Voidable only at the option of the government
mcqs.answer: Void as against claims enforceable under the attachment

mcqs.question: S.65 provides that where immovable property is sold in execution and the sale becomes absolute, the property is deemed to have vested in the purchaser from the:
options: Time when the property is sold, not from the time when the sale becomes absolute
mcqs.answer: Time when the property is sold, not from the time when the sale becomes absolute

mcqs.question: S.73A (or corresponding provision) and related rules address the priority of a decree-holder who has attached property before judgment as against subsequent attaching decree-holders; the general principle is that an:
options: Attachment before judgment does not create a charge but affects priority in rateable distribution as provided by law
Attachment before judgment gives absolute ownership
Attachment before judgment has no legal effect
There is no such provision in the Code
mcqs.answer: Attachment before judgment does not create a charge but affects priority in rateable distribution as provided by law

mcqs.question: If the original appeal is withdrawn or dismissed for default, a memorandum of cross-objections filed under Order XLI Rule 22 may nevertheless be:
options: Heard and determined on the merits
mcqs.answer: Heard and determined on the merits

mcqs.question: Abatement of appeals on the death of a party, where legal representatives are not brought on record within the prescribed time, is governed analogously to:
options: Order XXII (death, marriage, insolvency of parties)
mcqs.answer: Order XXII (death, marriage, insolvency of parties)
mcqs.reference: O.XXII, applicable to appeals via O.XLI/S.107

mcqs.question: S.107 confers upon the appellate court the power to determine a case finally, remand a case, frame issues and refer them for trial, and:
options: Take additional evidence or require such evidence to be taken
Grant fresh causes of action not pleaded
Ignore the trial court's judgment entirely without reason
mcqs.answer: Take additional evidence or require such evidence to be taken

mcqs.question: Under Order XXXVIII Rule 5, attachment before judgment may be ordered where the court is satisfied that the defendant, with intent to obstruct or delay execution of any decree, is about to:
options: Dispose of the whole or part of his property, or remove it from the jurisdiction of the court
mcqs.answer: Dispose of the whole or part of his property, or remove it from the jurisdiction of the court

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII Rule 1 empowers the court, at any stage of a suit, to order arrest and require security from a defendant who is about to abscond or leave the jurisdiction with intent to:
options: Delay or obstruct execution of any decree that may be passed against him
mcqs.answer: Delay or obstruct execution of any decree that may be passed against him

mcqs.question: The principle that an executing court cannot go behind the decree means that it generally cannot question the:
options: Correctness or validity of the decree on its merits
Applicability of limitation to the execution application
mcqs.answer: Correctness or validity of the decree on its merits

mcqs.question: S.96(4) and related provisions restrict the right of appeal in small cause suits, and revision from such decrees is governed by the:
options: Small Cause Courts Act along with relevant CPC provisions
CPC alone with no special statute
mcqs.answer: Small Cause Courts Act along with relevant CPC provisions

mcqs.question: Costs incurred in the process of execution are recoverable as part of the execution proceedings, and the executing court has discretion regarding such costs under provisions analogous to:
mcqs.answer: S.35 (costs)

mcqs.question: Execution of a decree against the Government or a public officer in respect of acts done in official capacity is subject to special procedural safeguards, including the requirement that the decree specify a time period, and is governed alongside:

mcqs.topic: Execution - Decree for Specific Movable Property
mcqs.question: Execution of a decree for any specific movable property is governed by:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 31

mcqs.question: Execution of a decree for an injunction, where a party disobeys, allows the court to enforce it by attachment of property, and, if necessary, by detention in civil prison, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 32

mcqs.question: Execution of a decree for partition of immovable property assessed to payment of revenue to the government is governed by:
options: Order XXI Rule 35 and related revenue law provisions
Order XX Rule 18 alone without execution rules
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 35 and related revenue law provisions

mcqs.question: Where the memorandum of appeal is not accompanied by a copy of the judgment/decree as required, or does not conform to Order XLI Rule 1, the appellate court may reject or return it, or allow the appellant to:
options: Amend it within a time to be fixed by the court
Never amend it under any circumstances
Convert it into a revision automatically
mcqs.answer: Amend it within a time to be fixed by the court

mcqs.question: An appellate court, before granting stay of execution, may require the appellant to give security for the due performance of the decree, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XLI Rule 5(3)

mcqs.question: Order XLI Rule 31 requires the judgment of the appellate court to state the points for determination, the decision thereon, the reasons for the decision, and:
options: Where the decree appealed from is reversed or varied, the relief to which the appellant is entitled
Only the final order without reasons
mcqs.answer: Where the decree appealed from is reversed or varied, the relief to which the appellant is entitled

mcqs.question: An objection that an execution application is time-barred is a question falling under:
options: S.47 (to be determined by the executing court)
mcqs.answer: S.47 (to be determined by the executing court)

mcqs.question: Order XXIII Rule 1 allows the plaintiff to withdraw a suit or abandon part of a claim, and, with the court's permission, to withdraw with liberty to institute a fresh suit if:
options: The suit must fail by reason of some formal defect, or there are sufficient grounds for allowing the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit
He simply wishes to file it in another jurisdiction
The defendant has not filed a written statement
It is more than five years since institution
mcqs.answer: The suit must fail by reason of some formal defect, or there are sufficient grounds for allowing the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit

mcqs.question: A compromise of a suit, to be recorded and a decree passed in accordance with it, must be in writing and signed by the parties, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXIII Rule 3

mcqs.question: Order XXII Rule 1 provides that the death of a plaintiff or defendant shall not cause the suit to abate if the right to sue:
mcqs.answer: Survives

mcqs.question: Where the right to sue survives, but no application to bring the legal representatives of a deceased plaintiff/defendant on record is made within the time limited by law, the suit shall:
options: Abate so far as the deceased party is concerned
Be referred to the High Court Division
mcqs.answer: Abate so far as the deceased party is concerned

mcqs.question: An application to set aside abatement, or for substitution of legal representatives after limitation, may be made on showing sufficient cause, under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXII Rule 9

mcqs.question: Order XXV empowers the court to require a plaintiff to give security for costs of the defendant, particularly where the plaintiff resides outside Bangladesh and possesses no sufficient property within it, and failure to furnish security may result in:
options: Automatic decree in favour of the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Dismissal of the suit

mcqs.question: A commission to examine a witness who is unable to attend the court due to sickness or infirmity may be issued under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXVI Rule 1

mcqs.question: A commission for local investigation, e.g. to elucidate matters in dispute or to ascertain market value/mesne profits/damages, may be issued under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXVI Rule 9

mcqs.question: Order XXIX deals with suits by or against corporations, allowing pleadings to be signed and verified, and process served, on behalf of the corporation by:
options: The secretary or any director or other principal officer who is able to depose to the facts of the case
mcqs.answer: The secretary or any director or other principal officer who is able to depose to the facts of the case

mcqs.question: Order XXXIV deals with suits relating to mortgages of immovable property, and provides for a preliminary decree for foreclosure, sale, or redemption before a:
mcqs.answer: Final decree is passed

mcqs.question: Order XXXVII provides a summary procedure for suits based upon negotiable instruments and certain other classes of suits, under which the defendant must obtain:
options: Automatic right to defend without leave
No right to defend at all
mcqs.answer: Leave to defend

mcqs.question: S.141 provides that the procedure in the Code applies, so far as it can be made applicable, to proceedings other than suits or appeals, subject to certain exclusions clarified by explanation regarding:
options: Proceedings under Article 226/writ or similar constitutional/special jurisdiction (interpreted narrowly)
mcqs.answer: Proceedings under Article 226/writ or similar constitutional/special jurisdiction (interpreted narrowly)

mcqs.question: S.145 provides that where a person has become surety for the performance of a decree or for restitution of property, he may be proceeded against under the Code:
options: In the same manner as a judgment-debtor
Never; sureties are outside the Code
mcqs.answer: In the same manner as a judgment-debtor

mcqs.question: S.146 provides that where any proceeding may be taken or application made by or against any person, it may equally be taken or made by or against:
options: Only his legal heirs after death
mcqs.answer: Any person claiming under him

mcqs.question: S.148A provides for the right to file a caveat, whereby a person may lodge a caveat and require notice before an order is passed against him in a proceeding which is instituted or:
mcqs.answer: Is expected to be instituted

mcqs.question: Order XLII Rule 2 requires that where a second appeal is preferred on the ground of an erroneous finding of fact, the memorandum of appeal must clearly state:
options: The substance of the evidence relating to the point and the finding upon it, so far as necessary
The value of the suit only
mcqs.answer: The substance of the evidence relating to the point and the finding upon it, so far as necessary

mcqs.question: Where property is attached in execution but the decree-holder does not proceed to take further steps within the prescribed time, the court may, on this ground, order the attachment to be:
options: Withdrawn or the application dismissed for default
mcqs.answer: Withdrawn or the application dismissed for default

mcqs.question: S.69 and related provisions deal with the doctrine of contribution among co-sharers whose joint property has been sold to satisfy a decree, entitling a co-sharer who has paid more than his share to:
mcqs.answer: Seek contribution from the others

mcqs.question: The mere filing of an appeal does not, by itself, operate as a:
options: Stay of the decree or execution proceedings
Nullification of the trial court's jurisdiction
mcqs.answer: Stay of the decree or execution proceedings

mcqs.question: Where a party had a remedy of appeal available but did not avail it, the High Court Division's revisional jurisdiction under S.115 will ordinarily:
options: Not be exercised as a substitute for an appeal not filed
Be mandatory in every such case
mcqs.answer: Not be exercised as a substitute for an appeal not filed

mcqs.question: Under S.2(1), 'code' includes:
mcqs.answer: Rules

mcqs.question: S.2(4) defines 'district' as the local limits of the jurisdiction of a:
options: Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction (District Judge) and includes local limits of ordinary original civil jurisdiction of a High Court Division
mcqs.answer: Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction (District Judge) and includes local limits of ordinary original civil jurisdiction of a High Court Division

mcqs.question: S.2(5) defines 'foreign court' as a court situated:
options: Outside Bangladesh and not established or continued by the authority of the Government
mcqs.answer: Outside Bangladesh and not established or continued by the authority of the Government

mcqs.question: S.2(6) defines a 'foreign judgment' as the judgment of a:
mcqs.answer: Foreign court

mcqs.question: 'Legal representative' under S.2(11) means a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased, and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character, the person on whom the estate:
options: Devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued
mcqs.answer: Devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued

mcqs.question: S.2(13) defines 'movable property' as including:
options: Standing timber attached to earth, in all circumstances
mcqs.answer: Growing crops

mcqs.question: S.2(16) defines a 'public officer' to include, among others, every judge, every officer of court, every officer whose duty is to prevent offences, and every officer in the:
options: Service or pay of the Government or remunerated by fees/commission for the performance of public duty
mcqs.answer: Service or pay of the Government or remunerated by fees/commission for the performance of public duty

mcqs.question: S.2(17) defines 'rules' as rules and forms contained in the:
options: First Schedule or made under S.122 or S.125
mcqs.answer: First Schedule or made under S.122 or S.125

mcqs.question: S.2(9) 'judgment' is distinguished from a 'decree' primarily in that judgment is the:
options: Statement of grounds, while a decree is the formal expression of the adjudication
A verbal announcement only, not reduced to writing
mcqs.answer: Statement of grounds, while a decree is the formal expression of the adjudication

mcqs.question: A decree may be partly preliminary and partly final; an example commonly cited is a suit for:
options: Accounts, where the amount due is ascertained by further inquiry, or a suit for possession with mesne profits
mcqs.answer: Accounts, where the amount due is ascertained by further inquiry, or a suit for possession with mesne profits

mcqs.question: For a decision of a court to be a 'decree', it must, among other things, be an adjudication which conclusively determines the:
options: Rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit
mcqs.answer: Rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit

mcqs.question: 'Cause of action' is not defined in the Code, but is judicially understood as the bundle of essential facts:
options: Necessary for the plaintiff to prove before he can succeed
Necessary for the defendant to prove
mcqs.answer: Necessary for the plaintiff to prove before he can succeed
mcqs.reference: Judicial interpretation, relevant to O.VII R.1

mcqs.question: Territorial jurisdiction, pecuniary jurisdiction, and jurisdiction over the subject matter are the three broad kinds of jurisdiction a court must possess to competently try a suit; a decree passed by a court lacking:
options: Pecuniary or territorial jurisdiction is not automatically a nullity unless there was also a failure of justice, but lack of subject-matter jurisdiction renders it a nullity
Any of the three is always valid
Territorial jurisdiction is always void, without exception
Subject matter jurisdiction can be cured by consent
mcqs.answer: Pecuniary or territorial jurisdiction is not automatically a nullity unless there was also a failure of justice, but lack of subject-matter jurisdiction renders it a nullity

mcqs.question: S.15 CPC requires every suit to be instituted in the court of the:
options: Lowest grade competent to try it
mcqs.answer: Lowest grade competent to try it

mcqs.question: A decree passed in contravention of S.15 (institution in lowest competent court) is:
options: Not void merely on that ground, as S.99 saves it absent failure of justice
Void only if the value exceeds a certain amount
mcqs.answer: Not void merely on that ground, as S.99 saves it absent failure of justice

mcqs.question: S.17 provides that where a suit is to obtain relief in respect of, or compensation for wrong to, property situate within the jurisdiction of different courts, the suit may be instituted in any court within whose jurisdiction:
options: Any portion of the property is situate
The cause of action first arose only
mcqs.answer: Any portion of the property is situate

mcqs.question: S.18 addresses the situation where it is uncertain within which of two or more courts local limits any property is situate; in such a case, any one of those courts may, upon the statement of the fact being recorded, proceed to entertain and dispose of the suit relating to that property, subject to any objection that:
options: It has no jurisdiction, in which case it can transfer the record to the proper court
No objection can ever be raised
Only the High Court Division can decide the question of situs
mcqs.answer: It has no jurisdiction, in which case it can transfer the record to the proper court

mcqs.question: S.20 (residuary provision) provides that, subject to limitations, every suit shall be instituted in a court within whose local jurisdiction the defendant resides/carries on business/personally works for gain, or where the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises:
options: Whichever the plaintiff chooses among those available
Only where the cause of action wholly arises
Only in the court nearest to the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Whichever the plaintiff chooses among those available

mcqs.question: S.20 Explanation clarifies that a corporation is deemed to carry on business at its:
options: Sole or principal office in Bangladesh, and also, in respect of a cause of action arising at a place where it has a subordinate office, at such place
Head office of its parent company
Place of incorporation only, irrespective of operations
mcqs.answer: Sole or principal office in Bangladesh, and also, in respect of a cause of action arising at a place where it has a subordinate office, at such place

mcqs.question: S.21A (as introduced by amendment) bars a suit to set aside a decree passed in a former suit, between the same parties, on an objection as to the place of suing, subject to conditions similar to:

S.22 permits a defendant, where a suit could have been instituted in any one of two or more courts and is instituted in one of them, to apply for the suit to be transferred to another such court, and the power to order this transfer rests with the:
options: Appellate court to which the court in which the suit is brought is subordinate
mcqs.answer: Appellate court to which the court in which the suit is brought is subordinate

mcqs.question: S.23 specifies which court is empowered to determine an application for transfer under S.22 depending on whether the courts in question are subordinate to the same or different appellate courts; if to different High Court Divisions... (Note: reflects general structure)
options: The application is decided at the appropriate appellate level as prescribed
There is no rule; any court may decide
Only the Supreme Court decides in all cases
mcqs.answer: The application is decided at the appropriate appellate level as prescribed

mcqs.question: S.24 empowers the High Court Division or the District Court to transfer any suit, appeal or other proceeding pending before it for trial or disposal to any court subordinate to it, and to:
options: Withdraw any such case and either try/dispose of it or transfer it for trial to another competent court
mcqs.answer: Withdraw any such case and either try/dispose of it or transfer it for trial to another competent court

mcqs.question: S.25 empowers the Supreme Court, on application, to transfer any suit, appeal or proceeding from a court in one part of Bangladesh to a court in another, if satisfied that such transfer is:
options: Expedient for the ends of justice
Requested by the majority of witnesses
mcqs.answer: Expedient for the ends of justice

mcqs.question: S.26 provides that every suit shall be instituted by the presentation of a plaint, or in such other manner as may be prescribed, and every plaint shall comply with the rules contained in:
mcqs.answer: Orders IV and VII

mcqs.question: S.27 provides that where a suit has been duly instituted, a summons may be issued to the defendant to appear and answer the claim on a day to be therein specified, and provides that such summons may be served in:
options: The manner prescribed by rules (i.e., Order V)
Only by personal delivery by the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: The manner prescribed by rules (i.e., Order V)

mcqs.question: S.28 and S.29 deal respectively with service of summons where the defendant resides in another district and where he resides in a foreign territory (or outside Bangladesh), providing for transmission of summons to the:
options: Court within whose jurisdiction the defendant resides, for service
Foreign embassy only, without court involvement
Plaintiff's local court, which serves it directly abroad
mcqs.answer: Court within whose jurisdiction the defendant resides, for service

mcqs.question: S.30 empowers the court, at any time, either of its own motion or on application, to make orders regarding discovery, production and inspection of documents, and issue summonses to persons to attend and produce documents, and generally for the:
options: Purpose of enabling the suit to be fairly and completely disposed of, or of saving costs
mcqs.answer: Purpose of enabling the suit to be fairly and completely disposed of, or of saving costs

mcqs.question: S.32 empowers the court to compel attendance of any person to whom a summons has been issued and who fails to comply, by issuing a warrant for his arrest, attachment and sale of his property, or:
mcqs.answer: Imposition of a fine

mcqs.question: S.33 provides that the court, after the case has been heard, shall pronounce judgment, and on such judgment a decree shall follow:
options: Automatically without reference to the judgment
mcqs.answer: In accordance with the judgment

mcqs.question: Under S.34, the court's discretionary power to award pre-suit (pre-litigation) interest applies where there is an:
options: Agreement for payment of interest, or interest is payable by law/usage
No agreement at all, in every case
Only when the debt exceeds a fixed amount
mcqs.answer: Agreement for payment of interest, or interest is payable by law/usage

mcqs.question: Order I Rule 3 permits joinder of defendants where relief claimed is in respect of the same act or transaction and there is a common question of law or fact, similar in structure to the rule governing joinder of:
options: Causes of action under Order II Rule 3
mcqs.answer: Plaintiffs under Order I Rule 1

mcqs.question: Order I Rule 8 (representative suits) permits one or more persons to sue or be sued on behalf of all persons interested, where the persons interested are numerous, with the:
mcqs.answer: Permission of the court

mcqs.question: In a representative suit under Order I Rule 8, notice must be given to the persons interested by public advertisement or otherwise, as the court in each case may direct, mainly to ensure they are aware and can:
options: Apply to be made a party
Be exempted from the decree entirely
Ignore the outcome, since it does not bind them
mcqs.answer: Apply to be made a party

mcqs.question: Order I Rule 10(2) allows the court, at any stage of proceedings, to strike out any party improperly joined, or add any party whose presence before the court may be necessary to enable it to:
options: Effectually and completely adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in the suit
mcqs.answer: Effectually and completely adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in the suit

mcqs.question: A person added as a defendant under Order I Rule 10 is bound by proceedings from the date of the:
options: Order adding him as a party, not from the original date of institution, unless the court otherwise directs
Original institution of the suit always
mcqs.answer: Order adding him as a party, not from the original date of institution, unless the court otherwise directs

mcqs.question: Order III deals with recognized agents and pleaders, and provides that appearances, applications and acts required to be made or done by a party may be made or done by his recognized agent or by a:
mcqs.answer: Pleader appearing/acting on his behalf

mcqs.question: Order III Rule 2 defines 'recognized agents' to include persons holding powers of attorney authorized to make and do such appearances, applications and acts on behalf of such parties, and also includes:
options: Persons carrying on trade or business for and in the names of parties not resident within the local limits of the court's jurisdiction, in matters connected with such trade/business
Any random relative of the party
Every advocate enrolled in the country
mcqs.answer: Persons carrying on trade or business for and in the names of parties not resident within the local limits of the court's jurisdiction, in matters connected with such trade/business

mcqs.question: Order IV Rule 1 provides that every suit shall be instituted by presenting a plaint to the court or such officer as it appoints, and that the plaint shall comply with the rules contained in Orders VI and VII, so far as they are:
mcqs.answer: Applicable

mcqs.question: Order II Rule 1 requires that every suit shall, as far as practicable, be framed so as to afford ground for final decision upon the subjects in dispute and to prevent:
mcqs.answer: Further litigation concerning them

mcqs.question: Order II Rule 4 restricts the joinder of certain claims (e.g., claims for recovery of immovable property) with claims for mesne profits or damages for breach of contract, except with the:
options: Permission of the plaintiff's advocate alone
mcqs.answer: Leave of the court

mcqs.question: Order II Rule 5 prohibits the joinder of a claim by or against an executor, administrator or heir as such, with claims by or against him personally, unless the latter claims are:
options: Alleged to arise with reference to the estate in respect of which the plaintiff/defendant sues or is sued in a representative character
mcqs.answer: Alleged to arise with reference to the estate in respect of which the plaintiff/defendant sues or is sued in a representative character

mcqs.question: Order II Rule 6 empowers the court to order separate trials where the joinder of causes of action in one suit may embarrass or delay the trial, or is otherwise:
mcqs.answer: Inconvenient

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 1 defines 'pleading' as meaning a:
mcqs.answer: Plaint or written statement

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 3 provides that the forms in Appendix A of the First Schedule shall be used, when applicable, and where they are not applicable, forms of like character shall be:
options: Used, with such variations as circumstances may require
Disregarded in favour of foreign precedents
mcqs.answer: Used, with such variations as circumstances may require

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 5 empowers the court to order a party to strike out or amend any matter in a pleading which may be unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous or:
options: Vexatious, or which may tend to prejudice, embarrass or delay the fair trial of the suit
Consistent with the cause of action
mcqs.answer: Vexatious, or which may tend to prejudice, embarrass or delay the fair trial of the suit

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 14 requires every pleading to be signed by the party and his pleader, if any, and where the party is unable to sign it, it may be:
options: Signed by a person duly authorized by him to sign the same, or to sue or defend on his behalf
Left unsigned, since it is not mandatory
mcqs.answer: Signed by a person duly authorized by him to sign the same, or to sue or defend on his behalf

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 15 requires every pleading to be verified at the foot by the party or one of the parties, or by a person acquainted with the facts, stating which paragraphs he verifies of his own knowledge and which:
options: Upon information received and believed to be true
mcqs.answer: Upon information received and believed to be true

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 16 empowers the court to strike out or amend any matter in a pleading at any stage of the proceedings which is unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous or vexatious, or which is otherwise an abuse of the process of the:
mcqs.answer: Court

mcqs.question: Order VI Rule 17 (amendment of pleadings) requires that all amendments necessary for the purpose of determining the real questions in controversy be allowed, provided that no amendment shall be allowed after the trial has commenced unless the court concludes that:
options: In spite of due diligence, the party could not have raised the matter before the commencement of trial
Court fee has been fully paid
The amendment relates to a new cause of action, which is always allowed
mcqs.answer: In spite of due diligence, the party could not have raised the matter before the commencement of trial

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 2 requires that where the plaintiff seeks the recovery of money, the plaint shall state the:
options: Amount to be assessed by the court
mcqs.answer: Precise amount claimed

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 3 requires that where the subject-matter of the suit is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description sufficient to:
options: Identify the property, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement or survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers
Value the property at market rate
mcqs.answer: Identify the property, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement or survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 5 requires the plaint to show that the defendant is or claims to be interested in the subject matter, and that he is liable to be called upon to answer the plaintiff's:
mcqs.answer: Demand for relief

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 6 requires that where the suit is instituted after the expiration of the period prescribed by the Limitation Act, the plaint shall show the ground upon which:
options: Exemption from the law of limitation is claimed
The suit is filed at all
mcqs.answer: Exemption from the law of limitation is claimed

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 7 provides that every plaint shall state specifically the relief claimed, either simply or in the alternative, and it is not necessary to ask for:
options: General or other relief which may always be given as the court may think just, to the same extent as if it had been asked for
mcqs.answer: General or other relief which may always be given as the court may think just, to the same extent as if it had been asked for

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 9 deals with the procedure on admitting a plaint, directing the plaintiff to present copies for service on the defendant, and to pay the requisite fee for such service, within a time to be fixed by the:
mcqs.answer: Court

mcqs.question: Among the grounds for rejecting a plaint under Order VII Rule 11 are: it does not disclose a cause of action; the relief claimed is undervalued and the plaintiff fails to correct the valuation within a time fixed by the court; the plaint is insufficiently stamped and the plaintiff fails to supply the requisite stamp-paper within the time fixed; and:
options: The suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law
The defendant simply disputes the claim
The plaintiff is unable to prove his case at trial
mcqs.answer: The suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law

mcqs.question: For the purpose of deciding an application under Order VII Rule 11(a) (no cause of action), the court is generally confined to looking at:
options: The averments in the plaint alone (and documents relied upon), not the defence
Arguments of both counsel on facts outside the plaint
mcqs.answer: The averments in the plaint alone (and documents relied upon), not the defence

mcqs.question: Order VII Rule 14 requires that where a plaintiff sues upon a document in his possession or power, he shall produce it in court when the plaint is presented, and shall file a copy along with the plaint, described in a list to be:
mcqs.answer: Annexed to the plaint

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 2 requires the defendant to specifically plead grounds of defence which, if not raised, would take the plaintiff by surprise, or which raise issues of fact not arising out of the plaint, such as fraud, limitation, or:
mcqs.answer: Release

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 3 requires the defendant to specifically deal with each allegation of fact in the plaint, and a general denial of the grounds alleged is:
mcqs.answer: Not sufficient

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 5 provides that every allegation of fact in the plaint, if not denied specifically or by necessary implication, or stated to be not admitted in the pleading of the defendant, shall be taken to be:
options: Admitted, except as against a person under disability
mcqs.answer: Admitted, except as against a person under disability

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 6 requires that the sum claimed as a set-off must be an ascertained sum of money legally recoverable by the defendant from the plaintiff, not exceeding the pecuniary limits of the jurisdiction of the court, and both parties shall be deemed to occupy the position of:
options: Plaintiff and defendant respectively in a cross-suit as regards the set-off claimed
mcqs.answer: Plaintiff and defendant respectively in a cross-suit as regards the set-off claimed

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 6A (as introduced by amendment) permits a defendant to set up, by way of counter-claim, any right or claim in respect of a cause of action accruing to him against the plaintiff, either before or after filing of the suit, but before the defendant has:
options: Delivered his defence or before the time fixed for delivering his defence has expired
mcqs.answer: Delivered his defence or before the time fixed for delivering his defence has expired

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 9 provides that no pleading subsequent to the written statement of a defendant, other than by way of defence to a set-off or counter-claim, shall be presented except by the:
options: Written consent of the defendant only
Order of the appellate court exclusively
mcqs.answer: Leave of the court

mcqs.topic: Appearance & Consequences of Non-Appearance - Order IX
mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 1 requires the parties to appear before the court on the day fixed in the summons for the defendant to appear and answer, and Order IX Rule 2 provides that where the summons has not been served on the defendant due to the plaintiff's failure to pay costs for service, the court may:
options: Impose a fine on the plaintiff only
mcqs.answer: Dismiss the suit

mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 4 provides that where a suit is dismissed under Rule 2 or Rule 3, the plaintiff may (subject to law of limitation) bring a:
options: Fresh suit, or apply for an order to set the dismissal aside
Appeal only, never a fresh suit
Reference to the High Court Division
mcqs.answer: Fresh suit, or apply for an order to set the dismissal aside

mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 7 provides that where the court has adjourned the hearing ex-parte, and the defendant, at or before such hearing, appears and assigns good cause for his previous non-appearance, he may be heard in answer to the suit as if he had:
options: Appeared on the day fixed for his appearance
mcqs.answer: Appeared on the day fixed for his appearance

mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 9 provides that where a suit is wholly or partly dismissed under Rule 8 (for plaintiff's non-appearance, defendant not admitting), the plaintiff shall be precluded from bringing a fresh suit in respect of the same cause of action, but he may apply for an order to set aside the dismissal, if he satisfies the court that there was:
mcqs.answer: Sufficient cause for his non-appearance

mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 13 (setting aside ex-parte decree) provides that where the court is satisfied that the summons was not duly served, or that the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing, it shall make an order setting aside the decree as against him, upon such terms as to:
options: Costs, payment into court or otherwise, as it thinks fit
mcqs.answer: Costs, payment into court or otherwise, as it thinks fit

mcqs.question: Order IX Rule 13 proviso clarifies that where the decree is of such a nature that it cannot be set aside as against such defendant only, it may be set aside as against:
options: All or any of the other defendants also
Only co-defendants who also applied within limitation
mcqs.answer: All or any of the other defendants also

mcqs.question: Where multiple defendants are sued, and one appears while others do not, and the suit proceeds, Order IX Rule 6 read with related rules generally means the plaintiff must prove his case against the:
options: Non-appearing defendants, even though the appearing defendant may not contest
No one, since the suit is dismissed
mcqs.answer: Non-appearing defendants, even though the appearing defendant may not contest

mcqs.question: Order III Rule 4 requires that no pleader shall act for any person in any court unless he has been appointed for the purpose by such person by a document in writing signed by such person, called a:
mcqs.answer: Vakalatnama or memorandum of appearance

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 1 provides that when a suit is duly instituted, a summons may be issued to the defendant to appear and answer the claim, and to file the written statement of his defence, if any, within:
options: Thirty days from the date of service of summons on that defendant
mcqs.answer: Thirty days from the date of service of summons on that defendant

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 9 provides for service of summons by the court, ordinarily through its officer or by post, and Order V Rule 9A permits the plaintiff, at his own option, to:
options: Effect service of summons through a courier service or by registered post, as permitted
Serve summons personally without any authorization
Never serve summons himself under any process
Only use publication in a newspaper
mcqs.answer: Effect service of summons through a courier service or by registered post, as permitted

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 12 requires that, wherever practicable, service of summons shall be made on the defendant in person, unless he has an agent empowered to accept service, in which case service on such agent shall be:
options: Valid only with court's separate order each time
mcqs.answer: Sufficient

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 17 provides that where the defendant or his agent refuses to sign an acknowledgment of service, or cannot be found, and there is no other person to whom the summons can be delivered, the serving officer shall affix a copy of the summons on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the house, and then return the original to:
options: The court, with a report endorsing the circumstances
mcqs.answer: The court, with a report endorsing the circumstances

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 19 requires the serving officer's report of service to be verified by his affidavit, and where the court is satisfied that service was effected properly, it shall:
options: Declare that the summons has been duly served
Refer the report to the appellate court
Refuse to declare service in every case
mcqs.answer: Declare that the summons has been duly served

mcqs.question: Order V Rule 20 (substituted service) permits the court, where it is satisfied that the defendant is keeping out of the way to avoid service, or that for any other reason summons cannot be served in the ordinary way, to order service by affixing a copy at the courthouse and at some conspicuous part of the defendant's residence, and also, if the court thinks fit, by:
