options: Publication in a newspaper circulating in the locality
Sending it to a relative abroad only
Publishing it in the court's internal notice board only
mcqs.answer: Publication in a newspaper circulating in the locality

mcqs.question: Substituted service ordered and effected under Order V Rule 20 is deemed to be as effectual as if it had been made on the defendant:
options: Never; it remains a lesser form of service
Only if the defendant later admits receiving it
mcqs.answer: Personally

mcqs.question: Order X Rule 1 requires the court, at the first hearing of the suit, to ascertain from each party or his pleader whether he admits or denies such allegations of fact as are made in the plaint or written statement (if any) of the:
options: Opposite party, and are not expressly or by necessary implication admitted or denied
mcqs.answer: Opposite party, and are not expressly or by necessary implication admitted or denied

mcqs.question: Order X Rule 2 empowers the court to examine a party appearing in person, or present in court, or a person able to answer any material question relating to the suit, and such examination may be done by the court:
options: Orally, and the substance shall be reduced to writing
Only in writing submitted by the party
Only through cross-examination by the opposing party
mcqs.answer: Orally, and the substance shall be reduced to writing

mcqs.question: Order XI Rule 6 permits either party to apply for an order directing the other party to make discovery on oath of documents which are or have been in his possession or power, relating to any matter in:
options: The pleadings of a third party
mcqs.answer: Question in the suit

mcqs.question: Order XI Rule 12 permits either party to apply, without filing any affidavit, for an order directing any other party to make discovery on oath of the documents which are or have been in his possession or power relating to any matter in question, this being distinct from the interrogatories procedure under:
mcqs.answer: Order XI Rule 1

mcqs.question: Order XI Rule 21 provides that where a party fails to comply with an order for discovery or interrogatories, he is liable, if a plaintiff, to have his suit dismissed for want of prosecution, or, if a defendant, to have his defence:
options: Struck out, and to be placed in the same position as if he had not defended
mcqs.answer: Struck out, and to be placed in the same position as if he had not defended

mcqs.question: Order XII Rule 2 permits a party to call upon the other party, by notice, to admit any document, saving the costs of proving it, and if he refuses or neglects to admit within a stated time, the costs of proving the document shall be paid by him, whatever the result of the suit, unless the court:
options: Refers the matter to the appellate court
Refuses to make any costs order
mcqs.answer: Otherwise directs

mcqs.question: Order XIII Rule 3 empowers the court to reject any document which it considers irrelevant or otherwise inadmissible, recording the grounds of such rejection, and this is distinct from mere admission for:
mcqs.answer: Marking as an exhibit

mcqs.question: Order XIII Rule 10 empowers the court, on the application of any party or of its own motion, to send for and inspect any document in the possession of a public officer, if it thinks that the interests of justice so require, subject to any privilege or:
options: Fee payment by the plaintiff only
mcqs.answer: Objection recognised by law

mcqs.question: Order XIV Rule 3 provides that material propositions for framing issues may be gathered from allegations made in the pleadings or in answers to interrogatories, or from the:
options: Contents of documents produced by either party
Personal opinion of the presiding judge alone
mcqs.answer: Contents of documents produced by either party

mcqs.question: Order XIV Rule 5 empowers the court, at any time before passing a decree, to amend issues or frame additional issues on such terms as it thinks fit, and all such amendments as may be necessary for determining the:
options: Real question or controversy between the parties shall be made
Court fee payable shall be made
mcqs.answer: Real question or controversy between the parties shall be made

mcqs.question: Order XVII Rule 1 (as amended) restricts the number of adjournments that may ordinarily be granted to a party during the hearing of a suit, subject to the court's discretion in cases of sufficient cause, reflecting a policy against:
options: Undue and repeated delay in disposal of suits
mcqs.answer: Undue and repeated delay in disposal of suits

mcqs.question: Order XVIII Rule 4 (as amended) provides that in every case, the examination-in-chief of a witness shall be on:
options: Affidavit, subject to cross-examination which may be taken either before the court or before a commissioner
Oral testimony only, in every case
Video recording without any format requirement
mcqs.answer: Affidavit, subject to cross-examination which may be taken either before the court or before a commissioner

mcqs.question: Order XVIII Rule 17 empowers the court, at any stage of a suit, to recall any witness who has been examined and put such questions as it thinks fit, this being an example of the court's:
options: Power to ensure a fair and complete trial
mcqs.answer: Power to ensure a fair and complete trial

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 1 requires the court, after the case has been heard, to pronounce judgment in open court, either at once or as soon thereafter as may be practicable, and where judgment is not pronounced at once, a date shall be:
options: Fixed for pronouncing it, of which due notice shall be given
mcqs.answer: Fixed for pronouncing it, of which due notice shall be given

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 4 requires that judgments of Courts of Small Causes need not contain more than the points for determination and the decision thereon, whereas judgments of other courts shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon, and the:
mcqs.answer: Reasons for such decision

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 5 requires the court, in suits involving several issues, to state its findings or decision, with reasons, on:
options: Each separate issue, unless the finding upon any one issue is sufficient for the decision of the suit
Only issues raised by the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Each separate issue, unless the finding upon any one issue is sufficient for the decision of the suit

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 7 provides that the decree shall bear the date of the day on which the:
options: Decree was signed by the pleader
mcqs.answer: Judgment was pronounced

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 12 deals with decrees for possession and mesne profits, allowing the court to pass a decree for possession together with an inquiry into mesne profits, either up to the date of the decree, or up to the date of:
options: Delivery of possession to the decree-holder, or a period not exceeding three years from the date of the decree, whichever first occurs
Ten years from the decree, without exception
mcqs.answer: Delivery of possession to the decree-holder, or a period not exceeding three years from the date of the decree, whichever first occurs

mcqs.question: Order XX Rule 18 deals with decrees in suits for partition of property or separate possession of a share therein, distinguishing between immovable property assessed to payment of revenue to government (where the court passes a preliminary decree) and other cases, where the court may pass a decree:
options: Declaring the rights of the parties and directing such partition or separation to be made
Only a final decree in every instance
No decree until revenue authorities certify
mcqs.answer: Declaring the rights of the parties and directing such partition or separation to be made

mcqs.question: The general scheme of the CPC 1908 is often summarized as consisting of the body of the Code (Sections 1-158, containing substantive/general provisions of a permanent character) and the:
options: First Schedule (Orders and Rules, which are more procedural/flexible and can be amended by High Court Division rules)
Second Schedule dealing with criminal procedure
Limitation Act appended as an annexure
Evidence Act appended as an annexure
mcqs.answer: First Schedule (Orders and Rules, which are more procedural/flexible and can be amended by High Court Division rules)
mcqs.reference: S.121-122, general structure of the Code

mcqs.question: Order XIX Rule 1 empowers the court to order that any particular fact or facts may be proved by affidavit, or that the affidavit of any witness may be read at the hearing, on such conditions as the court thinks:
mcqs.answer: Reasonable

mcqs.question: Order XIX Rule 3 requires affidavits to be confined to such facts as the deponent is able of his own knowledge to prove, except on interlocutory applications, on which statements of his:
options: Belief may be admitted, provided the grounds thereof are stated
Belief must be corroborated by two witnesses
mcqs.answer: Belief may be admitted, provided the grounds thereof are stated

mcqs.question: Order XXVI Rule 4 empowers the court to issue a commission for examination of any person who resides beyond the local limits of its jurisdiction, or who is about to leave such limits before the:
options: Date fixed for his examination in court
mcqs.answer: Date fixed for his examination in court

mcqs.question: A commission to examine a witness residing outside Bangladesh is issued under provisions similar to Order XXVI Rule 5, and the examination is conducted according to the law and practice of the:
options: Country/place in which the examination is to take place, unless the court otherwise directs
Bangladesh courts alone, regardless of location
mcqs.answer: Country/place in which the examination is to take place, unless the court otherwise directs

mcqs.question: Order XXVI Rule 10 requires the commissioner, after executing a commission for local investigation, to return it together with his evidence, report and other proceedings, and the report along with evidence, if any, becomes part of the:
options: Confidential file, never disclosed to parties
Appellate record only, not the trial record
mcqs.answer: Record of the suit

mcqs.question: Order XXVI Rule 11 (or corresponding rule) empowers the court to issue a commission for scientific investigation, and Order XXVI also provides for commissions to examine accounts, and to make a partition, reflecting the flexible, multi-purpose nature of the:
mcqs.answer: Commission power under S.75

mcqs.question: Order XXVII Rule 1 provides that in suits by or against the Government, the plaint or written statement shall be signed by such person as the Government may, by general or special order, appoint in this behalf, and shall be:
options: Verified by any person whom the Government may so appoint
Verified only by the Attorney General
Verified by the plaintiff personally in every case
mcqs.answer: Verified by any person whom the Government may so appoint

mcqs.question: Order XXVII Rule 5 provides that the court, before which any suit against the Government or a public officer proceeds, may, in its discretion, allow further time to enable the person representing the Government to:
options: Communicate with the Government and obtain instructions
mcqs.answer: Communicate with the Government and obtain instructions

mcqs.question: Order XXVII Rule 8 provides that no person shall, as a public officer, be ordered to satisfy any decree except out of the property belonging to him in his:
options: Personal capacity, unless the decree is expressly against the government/office he represents
Neither capacity, since public officers are immune
mcqs.answer: Personal capacity, unless the decree is expressly against the government/office he represents

mcqs.question: Order XXXIV and related provisions on mortgage suits classify mortgage suits broadly into suits for foreclosure, suits for sale, and suits for:
mcqs.answer: Redemption

mcqs.question: Order XXXIV Rule 2 deals with the preliminary decree in a suit for foreclosure, which directs an account to be taken of what is due to the plaintiff, and fixes a date by which the defendant must pay the amount found due, failing which he shall be:
options: Debarred from all right to redeem the property (foreclosed)
Entitled to compensation from the plaintiff
mcqs.answer: Debarred from all right to redeem the property (foreclosed)

mcqs.question: Order XXXIV Rule 4 deals with the preliminary decree in a suit for sale, directing an account to be taken and fixing a date for payment, and providing that if payment is not made, the mortgaged property, or a sufficient part of it, shall be:
mcqs.answer: Sold

mcqs.question: Order XXXIV Rule 7 deals with the preliminary decree in a suit for redemption, directing accounts and fixing a date for payment by the plaintiff-mortgagor, and providing that upon such payment, the defendant shall deliver documents and, if necessary, retransfer or:
mcqs.answer: Deliver possession of the property

mcqs.question: Order XXXII Rule 3 provides that where the defendant is a minor, the court, upon being satisfied of the fact of minority, shall appoint a proper person to be a:
mcqs.answer: Guardian for the suit

mcqs.question: Order XXXII Rule 6 requires that a next friend or guardian for the suit shall not, without leave of the court, receive any money or other movable property on behalf of a minor by way of:
options: Compromise, or under a decree/order in favour of the minor
Gift from a third party unrelated to the suit
Sale of the guardian's own property
mcqs.answer: Compromise, or under a decree/order in favour of the minor

mcqs.question: Order XXXII Rule 7 requires that no next friend or guardian for the suit shall, without leave of the court, enter into any agreement or compromise on behalf of a minor with reference to the suit, and any such agreement or compromise entered into without leave is:
options: Voidable against all parties other than the minor
Fully binding on the minor regardless
Automatically valid if the guardian acted in good faith
Irrelevant, since minors cannot be sued
mcqs.answer: Voidable against all parties other than the minor

mcqs.topic: Suits by Indigent Persons - Order XXXIII
mcqs.question: Order XXXIII Rule 1 defines an 'indigent person' as one who is not possessed of sufficient means (other than property exempt from attachment and the subject-matter of the suit) to pay the fee prescribed for the plaint, or, where no such fee is prescribed, is not entitled to property worth:
options: One thousand taka (or the prescribed threshold)
There is no monetary threshold at all
mcqs.answer: One thousand taka (or the prescribed threshold)

mcqs.topic: Suits by Indigent Persons - Order XXXIII
mcqs.question: Order XXXIII Rule 5 lists grounds on which the court shall reject an application to sue as an indigent person, including where it is not framed and presented in the prescribed manner, where the applicant is not an indigent person, or where his allegations show:
options: A minor discrepancy in valuation only
mcqs.answer: No cause of action

mcqs.topic: Suits by Indigent Persons - Order XXXIII
mcqs.question: Order XXXIII Rule 8 provides that where the application to sue as an indigent person is granted, it shall be deemed the plaint in the suit, and shall proceed as a suit instituted in the:
mcqs.answer: Ordinary manner

mcqs.topic: Suits by Indigent Persons - Order XXXIII
mcqs.question: Order XXXIII Rule 11 provides that where an indigent person succeeds in the suit, the court shall calculate the amount of court-fees which would have been paid, and such amount shall be recoverable by the:
options: Government from the party ordered to pay costs, or out of the subject-matter of the suit
No one; it is waived permanently
mcqs.answer: Government from the party ordered to pay costs, or out of the subject-matter of the suit

mcqs.question: Order XXXV Rule 1 requires that in every interpleader suit, the plaint shall state, in addition to other statements necessary for plaints, that the plaintiff claims no interest in the subject-matter in dispute other than for:
mcqs.answer: Charges or costs

mcqs.question: Order XXXV Rule 3 permits the court, if it appears at the first hearing that the plaintiff has no interest in the subject-matter beyond charges or costs, to discharge him from liability and order him:
options: Costs, and dismiss him from the suit
Struck off as a witness only
Held jointly liable with the defendants
mcqs.answer: Costs, and dismiss him from the suit

mcqs.question: S.88 clarifies that an interpleader suit lies where two or more persons claim adversely to one another the same debt, sum of money or other property, movable or immovable, from another person who claims no interest therein other than for charges or costs, and who is ready to pay or deliver it to the:
options: Rightful claimant as may be decided by the court
mcqs.answer: Rightful claimant as may be decided by the court

mcqs.question: Order XXXVII Rule 2 provides that in a suit under this order, the defendant is not entitled to defend the suit unless he enters an appearance, and, in default of appearance, the allegations in the plaint shall be deemed to be:
options: Admitted, and the plaintiff shall be entitled to a decree
mcqs.answer: Admitted, and the plaintiff shall be entitled to a decree

mcqs.question: Order XXXVII Rule 3 requires the defendant, if he wishes to defend, to apply for leave to defend within the prescribed time, and leave may be granted:
options: Unconditionally or subject to conditions, such as furnishing security
Never, once summons for judgment is served
mcqs.answer: Unconditionally or subject to conditions, such as furnishing security

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII Rule 2 provides that where a defendant, on being called upon by the court, fails to furnish security as required for arrest before judgment, the court may commit him to civil prison until the:
options: Decision of the suit, or, where a decree is passed against him, until its execution
End of his natural life, without exception
mcqs.answer: Decision of the suit, or, where a decree is passed against him, until its execution

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII Rule 5 provides that the court may direct the defendant, within a time fixed, to furnish security to the satisfaction of the court, or to produce and place at the disposal of the court, property or its value, or to appear and show cause why he should not furnish security; and if he fails, the court may order the property specified to be:
mcqs.answer: Attached

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII Rule 6 requires that before ordering attachment, the court shall, unless the delay would defeat the object of the attachment, direct the defendant to show cause, within a time fixed, why he should not:
mcqs.answer: Furnish security

mcqs.question: Order XXXVIII Rule 11 provides that where a plaintiff obtains a decree in a suit in which an order of attachment before judgment has been made, he shall not be precluded from applying for a further order of attachment in:
options: Any circumstance whatsoever, since the earlier order becomes permanent automatically
mcqs.answer: Execution of the decree

mcqs.question: Order XXXIX Rule 1 provides that a temporary injunction may be granted where it is proved by affidavit or otherwise that any property in dispute is in danger of being wasted, damaged or alienated by any party, or wrongfully sold in execution of a decree, or that the:
options: Defendant threatens or intends to remove or dispose of his property with intent to defraud his creditors
Suit involves a large sum of money
Defendant has filed a written statement
mcqs.answer: Defendant threatens or intends to remove or dispose of his property with intent to defraud his creditors

mcqs.question: Order XXXIX Rule 2 empowers the court to grant a temporary injunction to restrain the defendant from committing a breach of contract or other injury of any kind to the plaintiff, where such breach/injury is:
options: Only actually committed, never merely threatened
mcqs.answer: Threatened or actually committed

mcqs.question: Order XXXIX Rule 3 requires the court, before granting an injunction, ordinarily to direct notice to be given to the opposite party, but it may grant an ex-parte injunction if it appears that the object of granting the injunction would be defeated by:
mcqs.answer: Delay

mcqs.question: Order XXXIX Rule 4 provides that an order for injunction may be discharged, varied or set aside by the court, on application made by any party dissatisfied with such order, and where the injunction has been granted without giving notice, the court shall, in appropriate cases:
options: Finally dispose of the application within a specified short period
Refer it to the High Court Division mandatorily
mcqs.answer: Finally dispose of the application within a specified short period

mcqs.question: Order XL Rule 1 empowers the court, where it appears just and convenient, to appoint a receiver of any property, and to remove any person from possession or custody of it, and confer upon the receiver powers to:
options: Collect rents and profits, and manage the property
Sell the property outright without any order
mcqs.answer: Collect rents and profits, and manage the property

mcqs.question: Order XL Rule 3 requires every receiver to furnish security, account as directed, pay the amount due from him as directed, and be responsible for any:
options: Loss occasioned by his wilful default or gross negligence
Loss under any circumstances, however caused
No responsibility whatsoever, since he acts as an officer of court
Loss caused only by the parties, never by himself
mcqs.answer: Loss occasioned by his wilful default or gross negligence

mcqs.question: A receiver appointed by the court is generally regarded as an officer of the:
options: Court, acting on its behalf and under its directions
mcqs.answer: Court, acting on its behalf and under its directions

mcqs.question: A key distinction between a decree and an order is that every decree is appealable unless expressly barred, whereas an order is appealable:
options: Only if specifically provided for under S.104 or Order XLIII
Only with leave of the Appellate Division
mcqs.answer: Only if specifically provided for under S.104 or Order XLIII

mcqs.question: Unlike a decree, which conclusively determines the rights of parties on the matters in controversy, an order:
options: May or may not finally determine such rights
Can never be passed in an interlocutory application
Must always follow a full trial
mcqs.answer: May or may not finally determine such rights

mcqs.question: Every decree is normally preceded by a judgment, but every judgment does not necessarily result in a decree, because a judgment may also form the basis of an:
mcqs.answer: Order

mcqs.question: The doctrine of res judicata under S.11 is based on three maxims, one of which is 'interest reipublicae ut sit finis litium', meaning:
options: It is in the interest of the state that there should be an end to litigation
No one should be made a judge in his own cause
He who comes to equity must come with clean hands
mcqs.answer: It is in the interest of the state that there should be an end to litigation

mcqs.question: For res judicata to apply, the former suit must have been decided by a court competent to try the:
options: Subsequent suit, or the suit in which the issue is subsequently raised
Any suit whatsoever, regardless of pecuniary jurisdiction
Only suits of the same value
mcqs.answer: Subsequent suit, or the suit in which the issue is subsequently raised

mcqs.question: Res judicata differs from the rule of estoppel in that res judicata results from a decision of a court, ousting the jurisdiction of another court to try the same issue again, while estoppel:
options: Is a rule of evidence which prevents a party from denying a fact he earlier represented, and does not bar the court's jurisdiction
Also bars a court's jurisdiction in the same way
Applies only after a decree is confirmed by the appellate court
mcqs.answer: Is a rule of evidence which prevents a party from denying a fact he earlier represented, and does not bar the court's jurisdiction
mcqs.reference: Conceptual distinction (S.11 CPC vs S.115 Evidence Act)

mcqs.question: Constructive res judicata under Explanation IV to S.11 bars a plea which:
options: Might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence in the former suit, but was not
Was actually raised and rejected in the former suit
Arose after the former suit was decided
Relates to a completely different cause of action
mcqs.answer: Might and ought to have been made a ground of attack or defence in the former suit, but was not

mcqs.question: Explanation VI to S.11 (res judicata between co-defendants) requires that there was a conflict of interest between the co-defendants, it was necessary to decide that conflict to grant relief to the plaintiff, and the:
options: Question was heard and finally decided between them
Plaintiff withdrew the claim against one co-defendant
Court refused to frame any issue
mcqs.answer: Question was heard and finally decided between them

mcqs.question: A decree passed by a court lacking inherent jurisdiction over the subject-matter is:
options: A nullity, void, and its invalidity can be set up whenever and wherever it is sought to be enforced or relied upon, including in execution
Merely voidable, and binding until set aside on appeal
Fully valid, since a decree cannot be questioned collaterally under any circumstances
Curable simply by consent of parties after the decree
mcqs.answer: A nullity, void, and its invalidity can be set up whenever and wherever it is sought to be enforced or relied upon, including in execution
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (jurisdictional nullity doctrine, cf. S.9, S.11, S.21)

mcqs.question: A decree obtained by fraud is generally considered:
options: Voidable, and can be challenged in a separate suit or appropriate proceeding on the ground of fraud
Automatically void ab initio without need for any challenge
Immune from challenge, since fraud vitiates only future transactions
Enforceable against everyone except the party defrauded
mcqs.answer: Voidable, and can be challenged in a separate suit or appropriate proceeding on the ground of fraud
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (fraud vitiates judicial proceedings, judicial interpretation)

mcqs.question: S.10 (stay of suit / res sub judice) differs from S.11 (res judicata) in that S.10 applies where the previously instituted suit is still:
options: Pending, whereas S.11 applies where the former suit has already been decided
Decided, whereas S.11 applies to pending suits
Filed in a foreign court exclusively
Filed by the same plaintiff only, never a different one
mcqs.answer: Pending, whereas S.11 applies where the former suit has already been decided

mcqs.question: For S.10 to apply, the matter in issue in the subsequently instituted suit must be directly and substantially in issue in the previously instituted suit, and both suits must be between the same parties or their representatives, litigating under the same title, in courts having jurisdiction to grant the relief claimed, and the previously instituted suit must be pending in the:
options: Same court, a different court in Bangladesh, or even a competent court outside Bangladesh established by government, subject to conditions
Same district only, with no exception
Same bench of the same court only
mcqs.answer: Same court, a different court in Bangladesh, or even a competent court outside Bangladesh established by government, subject to conditions

mcqs.question: Where a matter has been finally decided by a competent civil court, the principle of res judicata (or its underlying policy) is generally applied by analogy to bar re-agitation of the same issue in a subsequent:
options: Writ petition or other proceeding between the same parties on the same cause of action
Criminal trial for an unrelated offence
Arbitration on an entirely different contract
Tax assessment for a different year, on unrelated facts
mcqs.answer: Writ petition or other proceeding between the same parties on the same cause of action
mcqs.reference: General principle extending S.11's policy (judicial interpretation)

mcqs.topic: Concept - Cause of Action & Order II Rule 2 Bar
mcqs.question: The bar under Order II Rule 2 (omission to sue for whole of claim) is often distinguished from res judicata under S.11 because Order II Rule 2 concerns the:
options: Same cause of action being split, rather than an issue already heard and decided
Same issue already decided in a former suit
mcqs.answer: Same cause of action being split, rather than an issue already heard and decided

mcqs.question: The maxim that 'consent cannot confer jurisdiction' generally means that where a court inherently lacks jurisdiction over the subject-matter, the parties cannot, by their agreement, invest it with:
options: Territorial jurisdiction, which they can waive
Pecuniary jurisdiction, which they can waive
mcqs.answer: Such jurisdiction

mcqs.question: Unlike lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, an objection as to pecuniary or territorial jurisdiction, if not raised at the earliest opportunity as required by S.21, is generally:
options: Waived, and cannot be raised for the first time in appeal or revision, absent failure of justice
Automatically fatal to the decree regardless of timing
Irrelevant to the outcome of the case
mcqs.answer: Waived, and cannot be raised for the first time in appeal or revision, absent failure of justice

mcqs.topic: Concept - Res Judicata and Interlocutory Orders
mcqs.question: The principle of res judicata generally does not strictly apply to interlocutory orders passed during the pendency of the same suit, but courts often apply an analogous principle to prevent:
options: Re-agitation of the same interlocutory matter repeatedly within the same proceeding
Any appeal from the final decree
mcqs.answer: Re-agitation of the same interlocutory matter repeatedly within the same proceeding

mcqs.question: The principle that an 'executing court cannot go behind the decree' does not prevent the executing court from examining questions relating to the:
options: Executability of the decree, such as whether it is a nullity for want of inherent jurisdiction
Merits of the original controversy decided by the trial court
Correctness of findings of fact recorded in the judgment
Adequacy of the relief granted in the decree
mcqs.answer: Executability of the decree, such as whether it is a nullity for want of inherent jurisdiction

mcqs.question: Among appeal, reference, review, and revision, the remedy that is exercised by the same court which passed the decree/order, on grounds such as discovery of new evidence, is:
mcqs.answer: Review

mcqs.question: Among appeal, reference, review, and revision, the remedy exercised by a subordinate court referring a doubtful question of law to a superior court is:
mcqs.answer: Reference

mcqs.question: Among appeal, reference, review, and revision, the remedy that lies to a superior court to correct jurisdictional errors where no appeal is available is:
mcqs.answer: Revision

mcqs.question: Unlike review or revision, an appeal is generally a:
options: Continuation of the original suit, giving the appellate court the same powers as the trial court to re-examine facts and law
Wholly independent proceeding unconnected with the original suit
Remedy available only after review has been exhausted
Remedy available only to the government
mcqs.answer: Continuation of the original suit, giving the appellate court the same powers as the trial court to re-examine facts and law

mcqs.question: Inherent powers under S.151 cannot be exercised in a manner that is:
options: In conflict with what has been expressly provided for in the Code, or contrary to specific provisions
Beneficial to any party at all
Exercised at all, since S.151 is purely declaratory
mcqs.answer: In conflict with what has been expressly provided for in the Code, or contrary to specific provisions

mcqs.topic: Concept - Res Judicata and Consent Decree
mcqs.question: A consent decree generally operates as res judicata between the parties on matters actually settled by it, but its scope is usually construed:
options: Narrowly, based on the actual terms agreed, since it does not involve adjudication on the merits by the court
Broadly, exactly as if the court had adjudicated the merits after full trial
As having no binding effect on the parties whatsoever
As binding only on the government
mcqs.answer: Narrowly, based on the actual terms agreed, since it does not involve adjudication on the merits by the court

mcqs.question: Courts generally take a liberal approach to allowing amendment of pleadings before trial commences, guided by the principle that amendment should be allowed unless it causes:
options: Injustice to the other side that cannot be compensated by costs, or introduces a wholly new/inconsistent case altering the nature of the suit
A change in the relief sought, which is never permitted
An increase in court fees, which is barred
mcqs.answer: Injustice to the other side that cannot be compensated by costs, or introduces a wholly new/inconsistent case altering the nature of the suit

mcqs.question: An amendment that seeks to introduce a new cause of action after the expiry of the limitation period is generally:
options: Refused, unless it merely elaborates facts already pleaded and does not alter the cause of action
Allowed only in appeal, never in trial
Irrelevant, since limitation does not apply to amendments
mcqs.answer: Refused, unless it merely elaborates facts already pleaded and does not alter the cause of action

mcqs.question: The objection of 'multifariousness' in a suit relates to the improper joinder of:
options: Distinct causes of action or parties having no common interest, in one suit
mcqs.answer: Distinct causes of action or parties having no common interest, in one suit

mcqs.question: S.52 of the Transfer of Property Act (doctrine of lis pendens) is conceptually linked to CPC provisions on attachment and execution because it similarly aims to prevent a party from defeating the outcome of pending litigation by:
options: Transferring the suit property during pendency of the suit
mcqs.answer: Transferring the suit property during pendency of the suit

mcqs.question: An ex-parte decree passed against a defendant who was duly served but chose not to appear is:
options: A valid and binding decree, subject to being set aside only on grounds specified in Order IX Rule 13
Not enforceable in execution at all
Only enforceable after the defendant's written consent
mcqs.answer: A valid and binding decree, subject to being set aside only on grounds specified in Order IX Rule 13

mcqs.question: Abatement of a suit due to failure to bring legal representatives on record within limitation, under Order XXII, results in the suit being treated, for most purposes, as though it had:
options: Never been filed, insofar as the deceased party is concerned
Been decreed in favour of the plaintiff
Been decreed in favour of the defendant
mcqs.answer: Never been filed, insofar as the deceased party is concerned

mcqs.topic: Concept - Order I Rule 10 and Limitation
mcqs.question: Where a new defendant is added to a suit under Order I Rule 10 after the expiry of the limitation period applicable to him, the suit against him is generally:
options: Barred by limitation, unless it falls within a recognised exception (such as relation back in certain circumstances)
Automatically maintainable if he is a necessary party
mcqs.answer: Barred by limitation, unless it falls within a recognised exception (such as relation back in certain circumstances)
mcqs.reference: O.I R.10 read with Limitation Act (conceptual)

mcqs.question: A suit instituted in the name of an unregistered partnership firm, without complying with the applicable registration requirements under the Partnership Act, may face a bar under partnership law, distinct from procedural bars found in:
mcqs.answer: Order XXX of the CPC

mcqs.question: The doctrine of merger provides that where a decree of a trial court is confirmed, modified, or reversed by an appellate court, the decree of the trial court:
options: Merges into the decree of the appellate court
Continues to operate independently in every respect
Has no further legal significance whatsoever, even for limitation purposes
mcqs.answer: Merges into the decree of the appellate court
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (doctrine of merger, S.96/S.100 read with S.11 Expl.)

mcqs.topic: Concept - Doctrine of Merger and Limitation for Execution
mcqs.question: As a consequence of the doctrine of merger, the period of limitation for executing a decree that has been the subject of an appeal generally runs from the date of the:
options: Appellate decree, not the original trial court decree
mcqs.answer: Appellate decree, not the original trial court decree

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Order VII Rule 11 vs O.VI R.16
mcqs.question: While Order VII Rule 11 empowers rejection of the plaint on specified grounds (e.g., no cause of action, undervaluation, insufficient stamping, statutory bar), Order VI Rule 16 more broadly empowers the court to strike out pleadings that are:
options: Unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of process
mcqs.answer: Unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of process
mcqs.reference: O.VI R.16 vs O.VII R.11 (conceptual distinction)

mcqs.question: In a suit for partition where a preliminary decree has been passed declaring the shares of the parties, and before the final decree is passed, if a party dies, the proceedings for the final decree are generally:
options: Continued with the legal representatives of the deceased party being brought on record
mcqs.answer: Continued with the legal representatives of the deceased party being brought on record

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Withdrawal of Suit and Res Judicata
mcqs.question: Where a plaintiff withdraws a suit without obtaining the court's permission to file a fresh suit under Order XXIII Rule 1, he is precluded from instituting a fresh suit on the same cause of action, a bar which operates somewhat similarly in effect to:
options: Res judicata, though technically distinct in its statutory basis
Estoppel under S.115 of the Evidence Act only
Order II Rule 2 exclusively, with no independent basis
mcqs.answer: Res judicata, though technically distinct in its statutory basis

mcqs.question: A set-off under Order VIII Rule 6 is confined to an ascertained sum of money and must be legally recoverable at the date of filing the written statement, whereas a counter-claim under Order VIII Rule 6A can relate to a right or claim of a wider nature, including a claim for:
options: Unliquidated damages or other reliefs, not merely a sum of money
Nothing beyond a sum of money, exactly like set-off
mcqs.answer: Unliquidated damages or other reliefs, not merely a sum of money

mcqs.question: Courts generally decline to grant a temporary injunction where the applicant has an equally efficacious alternative remedy, such as:
options: Damages, which would adequately compensate him
No alternative remedy is ever considered relevant
The filing of a fresh suit only
mcqs.answer: Damages, which would adequately compensate him

mcqs.question: A prohibitory injunction restrains a party from doing a particular act, whereas a mandatory injunction:
options: Compels a party to perform a positive act to prevent breach of an obligation
Also merely restrains an act, with no positive obligation
Is available only in criminal proceedings
Cannot be granted under the CPC at any stage
mcqs.answer: Compels a party to perform a positive act to prevent breach of an obligation
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (O.XXXIX and Specific Relief Act principles)

mcqs.question: 'Balance of convenience' as a factor for grant of temporary injunction requires the court to weigh the:
options: Comparative mischief or inconvenience likely to be caused to each party by granting or refusing the injunction
Financial status of each party alone
Number of witnesses each party can produce
Seniority of the counsel appearing for each party
mcqs.answer: Comparative mischief or inconvenience likely to be caused to each party by granting or refusing the injunction

mcqs.question: An 'ad-interim' injunction is generally understood as an injunction granted:
options: For a short period, pending final disposal of the injunction application itself, often ex-parte
Permanently, with no further hearing required
Only after full trial of the suit
mcqs.answer: For a short period, pending final disposal of the injunction application itself, often ex-parte

mcqs.question: Appointment of a receiver under Order XL differs from attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII in that a receiver actively manages and preserves the property (e.g., collecting rents), whereas attachment merely:
options: Prohibits the judgment-debtor/defendant from transferring or dealing with the property
Also actively manages the property in the same way
Transfers ownership of the property to the decree-holder
Results in automatic sale of the property
mcqs.answer: Prohibits the judgment-debtor/defendant from transferring or dealing with the property

mcqs.question: Where a decree-holder has more than one mode of execution available for realizing his decree, he may be required, in certain circumstances, to elect between inconsistent remedies, reflecting the general:
options: Doctrine of estoppel by conduct exclusively
mcqs.answer: Doctrine of election

mcqs.question: The value of a suit for the purpose of court fees and the value for the purpose of jurisdiction may, in certain classes of suits (e.g., suits for injunction, declaration), be:
options: Different, as they are governed by different statutes and principles
Determined solely by the defendant's admission
mcqs.answer: Different, as they are governed by different statutes and principles
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (Court Fees Act vs S.15 CPC)

mcqs.question: A suit for a mere declaration of right or status, without consequential relief where such relief could be claimed, is generally barred under the:
options: Specific Relief Act (proviso to declaratory relief provisions)
mcqs.answer: Specific Relief Act (proviso to declaratory relief provisions)

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Res Judicata and Interim Orders on Injunction
mcqs.question: A finding at the interlocutory stage on a prima facie case for grant/refusal of temporary injunction is generally regarded as:
options: Tentative, and does not operate as res judicata at the final hearing of the suit
Final and binding as res judicata for the trial
Binding on the appellate court permanently
Irrelevant to the final decision of the suit
mcqs.answer: Tentative, and does not operate as res judicata at the final hearing of the suit

mcqs.question: The general principle 'costs follow the event' under S.35 means that costs are ordinarily awarded to the:
options: Successful party, though the court retains discretion to order otherwise for reasons recorded
Party who filed first, regardless of outcome
Losing party, as a matter of settled rule
mcqs.answer: Successful party, though the court retains discretion to order otherwise for reasons recorded

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Interim Application and Main Suit
mcqs.question: An order passed on an interlocutory application (e.g., temporary injunction) does not, as a general rule, finally decide the:
options: Question of costs of that application
Question of security, if any, imposed
mcqs.answer: Merits of the main suit
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (O.XXXIX and general interlocutory order principles)

mcqs.question: Under-valuation of a suit, if not corrected within the time fixed by the court under Order VII Rule 11(b), results in:
options: Automatic dismissal of the suit on merits
Transfer of the suit to a higher court without objection
mcqs.answer: Rejection of the plaint

mcqs.question: Where a plaintiff seeks both a declaration and consequential relief such as possession or injunction in one suit, this is generally permissible and does not offend the rule against:
options: Splitting of claims under Order II Rule 2
mcqs.answer: Splitting of claims under Order II Rule 2

mcqs.question: Order XXXV Rule 5 clarifies that the interpleader procedure does not apply where the person from whom the parties claim adversely to one another is already a defendant in a suit instituted by:
options: One of the claimants against him for the debt or property
A third party unconnected to the claim
No one; the rule has no such exception
mcqs.answer: One of the claimants against him for the debt or property

mcqs.question: In an interpleader suit, once the plaintiff is discharged upon depositing the property/money in court, the litigation continues essentially as a contest between the:
options: Rival claimants (defendants) as to who is entitled to the property/money
mcqs.answer: Rival claimants (defendants) as to who is entitled to the property/money

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Summary Suit Leave to Defend
mcqs.question: In summary suits under Order XXXVII, if the defendant satisfies the court that he has a substantial defence or raises a triable issue, leave to defend is ordinarily granted; but if his defence is illusory or moonshine, leave may be:
options: Irrelevant, since leave is never required
Granted only after full trial on merits
mcqs.answer: Refused, or granted only conditionally

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Suit Against Trustees - Order XXXI
mcqs.question: Order XXXI provides that in suits concerning trust property, it is generally sufficient to make the trustees, executors or administrators (as representing the trust) parties, without joining the beneficiaries, unless the court otherwise directs, reflecting the principle of:
options: Representative litigation for the benefit of the trust estate
Compulsory joinder of all beneficiaries in every trust suit
Exclusion of trustees from litigation entirely
Automatic abatement upon a trustee's death
mcqs.answer: Representative litigation for the benefit of the trust estate

mcqs.question: Order XXX (as extended by rules on associations) permits certain unincorporated associations to sue or be sued in their own name in specified circumstances, similar in structure to the treatment of:
options: Partnership firms under Order XXX Rule 1
mcqs.answer: Partnership firms under Order XXX Rule 1

mcqs.question: In a suit for rendition of accounts, the court typically passes a preliminary decree directing the defendant to render accounts, followed, after examination of accounts, by a:
options: Final decree for the amount found due
Single composite decree with no preliminary stage, in all such suits
Interim decree that never becomes final
Decision only on limitation, with accounts left unexamined
mcqs.answer: Final decree for the amount found due

mcqs.question: The 'doctrine of relation back', as applied to amendment of pleadings, generally means that an amendment, once allowed, relates back to the date of the:
options: Original pleading, unless the court directs otherwise
Order allowing the amendment only, never earlier
Filing of the written statement only
mcqs.answer: Original pleading, unless the court directs otherwise

mcqs.question: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is essentially a:
options: Procedural law (adjective law), as distinguished from substantive law which creates rights and liabilities
Substantive law creating new civil rights
mcqs.answer: Procedural law (adjective law), as distinguished from substantive law which creates rights and liabilities

mcqs.question: As a general rule, amendments to procedural law (such as the CPC) are presumed to apply:
options: Retrospectively, to pending proceedings as well, unless expressly or by necessary implication excluded
Only prospectively, never to pending suits
Never, since procedural amendments cannot affect pending cases
Only to suits filed before the amendment
mcqs.answer: Retrospectively, to pending proceedings as well, unless expressly or by necessary implication excluded

mcqs.question: Provisions of the CPC using the word 'shall' are not always construed as mandatory; courts examine the object and consequences of non-compliance to determine whether a provision is mandatory or merely:
mcqs.answer: Directory

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Order VII Rule 11 and Limitation
mcqs.question: Where a suit is ex facie barred by limitation on the face of the plaint itself, the court can reject the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) at the threshold, without requiring the defendant to:
options: File a written statement and go through a full trial
Appear at all in any capacity
mcqs.answer: File a written statement and go through a full trial

mcqs.topic: Interpretation - Second Appeal and Concurrent Findings
mcqs.question: Where the trial court and the first appellate court have both recorded the same finding of fact (concurrent findings), the High Court Division in second appeal will ordinarily not disturb such findings, unless they are shown to be:
options: Perverse, based on no evidence, or vitiated by a substantial question of law
Merely debatable on a fresh reading of the evidence
Different from the High Court Division's own personal view
Old, i.e., more than five years since the decree
mcqs.answer: Perverse, based on no evidence, or vitiated by a substantial question of law

mcqs.question: Where a special law (e.g., Artha Rin Adalat Ain, Family Courts Ordinance) provides its own specific procedure inconsistent with the CPC, the general principle is that the:
options: Special law prevails over the general provisions of the CPC to the extent of the inconsistency, with the CPC applying suppletively where the special law is silent
CPC always prevails over any special law
Special law is void for inconsistency with the CPC
Special law and CPC apply simultaneously with equal force, with no priority
mcqs.answer: Special law prevails over the general provisions of the CPC to the extent of the inconsistency, with the CPC applying suppletively where the special law is silent

mcqs.question: S.5 of the Limitation Act allows condonation of delay in filing an appeal, application (other than under Order XXI) or revision, if the applicant satisfies the court that he had:
options: Sufficient cause for not preferring it within the prescribed period
No cause at all, since delay is condoned automatically
A written apology to the opposite party
mcqs.answer: Sufficient cause for not preferring it within the prescribed period

mcqs.question: S.5 of the Limitation Act, by its own terms, does NOT apply to:
options: The filing of a suit, or an application under Order XXI of the CPC (execution applications)
mcqs.answer: The filing of a suit, or an application under Order XXI of the CPC (execution applications)

mcqs.question: S.12 of the Limitation Act provides that in computing the period of limitation for an appeal, revision or review, the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the:
options: Decree or order appealed from/sought to be revised/reviewed shall be excluded
mcqs.answer: Decree or order appealed from/sought to be revised/reviewed shall be excluded

mcqs.question: S.18 of the Limitation Act (concealment by fraud) postpones the commencement of the limitation period where the right to sue is concealed by fraud, and time begins to run only from when the plaintiff:
options: Discovers the fraud, or could with reasonable diligence have discovered it
Files the suit, regardless of discovery
Is served with a legal notice
mcqs.answer: Discovers the fraud, or could with reasonable diligence have discovered it

mcqs.question: S.6 of the Limitation Act provides that where a person entitled to institute a suit is, at the time from which the period of limitation is to be reckoned, a minor, insane, or an idiot, he may institute the suit after the disability ceases, within the:
options: Same period as would otherwise have been allowed from the time of cessation of disability
One year, regardless of the ordinarily applicable period
Ten years absolutely, regardless of disability
mcqs.answer: Same period as would otherwise have been allowed from the time of cessation of disability

mcqs.question: S.19 of the Limitation Act provides that where an acknowledgment of liability in respect of a right is made in writing, signed by the party or his agent, before the expiration of the prescribed period, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the:
options: Time when the acknowledgment was so signed
Original date the right accrued, unaffected by acknowledgment
mcqs.answer: Time when the acknowledgment was so signed

mcqs.question: For the purposes of limitation, a claim by way of set-off or counter-claim is treated as a separate suit, and is deemed to have been instituted, in the case of a set-off, on the date on which it is:
mcqs.answer: Pleaded in the written statement
mcqs.reference: Limitation Act (S.3 read with O.VIII R.6)

mcqs.question: An application for execution of a decree, other than a decree granting a mandatory injunction, is generally governed by Article of the Limitation Act prescribing a period of:
options: Twelve years from the date of the decree (subject to conditions, such as when the decree becomes enforceable, or the last payment/acknowledgment)
Three years, uniformly for every decree
mcqs.answer: Twelve years from the date of the decree (subject to conditions, such as when the decree becomes enforceable, or the last payment/acknowledgment)
mcqs.reference: Limitation Act, relevant Article for execution applications

mcqs.question: A suit for possession of immovable property based on title is generally governed by a limitation period of:
options: Twelve years from when the possession of the defendant becomes adverse to the plaintiff
Three years from the date of dispossession, uniformly
mcqs.answer: Twelve years from when the possession of the defendant becomes adverse to the plaintiff

mcqs.question: A suit for compensation for breach of a contract, where no specific period is otherwise prescribed, is generally governed by a limitation period of:
options: Three years from when the contract is broken
Six years, uniformly, with no exception
mcqs.answer: Three years from when the contract is broken

mcqs.question: Order XVIII Rule 4 (examination-in-chief by affidavit) operates alongside provisions of the Evidence Act relating to the manner of proving facts, but cross-examination and re-examination in respect of such affidavit evidence continue to be governed by the general principles of the:
mcqs.answer: Evidence Act
mcqs.reference: O.XVIII R.4 read with Evidence Act principles

mcqs.question: S.115 of the Evidence Act (estoppel) is conceptually distinct from res judicata under S.11 CPC, but both doctrines share the common underlying purpose of preventing:
options: A party from going back on a position previously represented or adjudicated, in appropriate circumstances
Any civil suit from being filed at all
mcqs.answer: A party from going back on a position previously represented or adjudicated, in appropriate circumstances
mcqs.reference: Conceptual (Evidence Act S.115 vs CPC S.11)

mcqs.question: Under Order XIII Rule 2, documents not produced, impounded or exhibited at the proper stage cannot ordinarily be relied on later without leave, a rule which operates alongside admissibility rules found in the:
mcqs.answer: Evidence Act
mcqs.reference: O.XIII R.2 read with Evidence Act

mcqs.question: Presumptions as to genuineness of certain documents (e.g., registered documents, certified copies) arise mainly under the Evidence Act, while the CPC (Order XIII) governs primarily the:
options: Procedure for production, admission and marking of documents as exhibits at trial
Substantive weight to be given to such documents
mcqs.answer: Procedure for production, admission and marking of documents as exhibits at trial

mcqs.question: The Court Fees Act, a separate statute, governs the fees payable on plaints, memoranda of appeal, and other documents, and interacts with the CPC chiefly through provisions such as:
options: Order VII Rule 11(b)/(c) on rejection of plaint for insufficient valuation/stamping
Order IX Rule 13 on setting aside ex-parte decrees
Order XXI Rule 90 on setting aside sales
mcqs.answer: Order VII Rule 11(b)/(c) on rejection of plaint for insufficient valuation/stamping
mcqs.reference: O.VII R.11 read with Court Fees Act

mcqs.question: For suits where relief cannot be precisely valued in monetary terms (e.g., certain injunction or declaratory suits), court fees are typically payable at a fixed rate prescribed under the:
options: Court Fees Act (Schedule provisions for such suits)
mcqs.answer: Court Fees Act (Schedule provisions for such suits)

mcqs.question: Where a plaint understates the value of the relief for the purpose of paying lower court fees, the court may require correction, and non-compliance leads to rejection of the plaint under:
mcqs.answer: Order VII Rule 11(b)

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 22 requires that notice be issued to the judgment-debtor before execution is ordered where the application for execution is made more than a specified period (commonly, one year) after the date of the decree, or against the legal representative of a party, primarily to:
options: Give the judgment-debtor or legal representative an opportunity to show cause against execution
Deny him any hearing at all
Transfer the case to another court
mcqs.answer: Give the judgment-debtor or legal representative an opportunity to show cause against execution

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 41 empowers the executing court, where a decree is for payment of money, to order the judgment-debtor, or, where he is a corporation, an officer thereof, to be examined as to what property he has, and how it is being dealt with, this being commonly known as examination of the judgment-debtor as to his:
mcqs.answer: Assets/means to satisfy the decree

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 64 empowers the court executing a decree to order sale of property attached, where necessary, but sale should generally be of only so much of the property as is:
options: Determined by the judgment-debtor's preference alone
Beyond what is needed, to allow surplus for the decree-holder's future claims
mcqs.answer: Necessary to satisfy the decree

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 72 restricts a decree-holder from purchasing property sold in execution of his own decree, without permission of the court, primarily to:
options: Prevent abuse and ensure a fair sale process, avoiding conflict of interest
Prevent any third-party purchaser from bidding
mcqs.answer: Prevent abuse and ensure a fair sale process, avoiding conflict of interest

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 84 requires that on every sale of immovable property, the person declared to be the purchaser shall pay immediately after such declaration a deposit of a percentage (commonly 25%) of the purchase money, and in default, the property is:
mcqs.answer: Resold

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 86 requires the full amount of the purchase money to be paid within a further specified period after the sale, failing which the deposit made under Rule 84 may be:
options: Forfeited to the government and the property resold
Refunded in full to the defaulting purchaser
Paid to the judgment-debtor as compensation only, with no resale
Transferred to the decree-holder as damages
mcqs.answer: Forfeited to the government and the property resold

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 94 provides that after a sale of immovable property has become absolute, the court shall grant a certificate specifying the property sold and the name of the person declared to be the:
options: Decree-holder, regardless of who purchased it
mcqs.answer: Purchaser

mcqs.question: Order XXI Rule 105 provides that where the applicant in execution proceedings does not appear on the day fixed for hearing, the court may dismiss the application, but may also, on sufficient cause shown within a prescribed time, restore it, similar in principle to:
options: Order IX (default and restoration for suits)
Order XLI Rule 11 (summary dismissal of appeal)
mcqs.answer: Order IX (default and restoration for suits)

mcqs.question: A plaintiff files a suit for recovery of a debt in a court whose pecuniary jurisdiction is exceeded by the claim value, and the defendant does not object at the earliest opportunity. On appeal, the defendant raises the pecuniary jurisdiction issue for the first time. Under S.21, this objection will most likely be:
options: Not entertained, since it was not raised at the earliest opportunity and no failure of justice is shown
Automatically fatal to the decree, since pecuniary jurisdiction can be raised at any time
Entertained only if the plaintiff consents
Referred compulsorily to the Appellate Division
mcqs.answer: Not entertained, since it was not raised at the earliest opportunity and no failure of justice is shown

mcqs.question: A previously filed suit for declaration of title between A and B was dismissed on merits after full trial. A now files a fresh suit against B for possession of the same property, based on the same title. B pleads res judicata. The plea will most likely:
options: Succeed, as the question of title was directly and substantially in issue and finally decided between the same parties
Fail, since possession and declaration are different reliefs, however related the underlying title question is
Fail automatically, because res judicata never applies between the same two individuals twice
Succeed only if A pays costs of the earlier suit first
mcqs.answer: Succeed, as the question of title was directly and substantially in issue and finally decided between the same parties

mcqs.question: A files a suit against B in the District Judge's Court for partition of property. While that suit is pending, A files a second suit against B in another court for the same relief regarding the same property. B applies to stay the second suit. The correct provision to invoke is:
options: O.II R.2 (omission to sue for the whole claim)
mcqs.answer: S.10 (stay of suit)

mcqs.question: A plaintiff files a suit for recovery of money that, on the face of the plaint, appears to have been filed 15 years after the cause of action arose, well beyond the applicable limitation period, and the plaint does not show any ground for exemption. The defendant, before filing a written statement, may apply for:
options: Rejection of the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d)
Dismissal for default under Order IX Rule 8
An ex-parte decree under Order IX Rule 6
mcqs.answer: Rejection of the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d)

mcqs.question: A defendant, though duly served with summons, fails to appear, and an ex-parte decree is passed against him. Two months later, he applies to set aside the decree, showing that he was seriously ill and hospitalized on the date of hearing, supported by medical records. The correct provision for such an application is:
options: Section 151 exclusively, since Order IX does not apply
mcqs.answer: Order IX Rule 13

mcqs.question: In a suit for recovery of Tk. 5,00,000, the defendant claims that the plaintiff owes him Tk. 2,00,000 under a separate, ascertained loan transaction, and wishes to adjust this amount against the plaintiff's claim. The appropriate procedural mechanism is:
options: Pleading a set-off under Order VIII Rule 6
Filing a fresh suit only, since adjustment within the same suit is not permitted
Filing an application under Order XXXIX for injunction
Filing an application under Order XI for discovery
mcqs.answer: Pleading a set-off under Order VIII Rule 6

mcqs.question: During the pendency of a suit for recovery of money, the plaintiff discovers that the defendant is selling off his assets and is likely to leave the country to avoid satisfying any future decree. The plaintiff's appropriate remedy is to apply for:
options: Attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII Rule 5
A decree under Order XX Rule 6 immediately, bypassing trial
Rejection of the defendant's written statement under Order VIII Rule 5
A commission under Order XXVI Rule 9
mcqs.answer: Attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII Rule 5

mcqs.question: X holds Tk. 10,00,000 in a fixed deposit, and both Y and Z separately claim entitlement to the entire sum, each asserting rights adverse to the other. X has no personal interest in the money other than to hand it over to the rightful claimant. X's appropriate remedy is to file:
options: An interpleader suit under Order XXXV and S.88
A suit for declaration under the ordinary procedure only
An application under Order XL for appointment of a receiver only
A suit for injunction restraining both Y and Z
mcqs.answer: An interpleader suit under Order XXXV and S.88

mcqs.question: A suit for partition of ancestral property is filed by one co-sharer against another, but a third co-sharer, whose share would necessarily be affected by any decree, is not made a party. The proper course for the court is to consider:
options: Adding the third co-sharer as a necessary party under Order I Rule 10
Dismissing the suit outright without any opportunity to add parties
Proceeding to decree the suit without regard to the third co-sharer's interest
Referring the matter for arbitration compulsorily
mcqs.answer: Adding the third co-sharer as a necessary party under Order I Rule 10

mcqs.question: During trial, after the plaintiff's evidence has closed, the plaintiff seeks to amend the plaint to introduce an entirely new and inconsistent cause of action that could have been pleaded at the outset with due diligence. The court will most likely:
options: Refuse the amendment, applying the proviso to Order VI Rule 17
Allow the amendment automatically, since amendments are always permitted
Allow the amendment only if the defendant is a minor
Refer the matter for revision to the High Court Division automatically
mcqs.answer: Refuse the amendment, applying the proviso to Order VI Rule 17

mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor dies after a money decree is passed against him but before it is fully satisfied. The decree-holder wishes to continue execution. He should proceed against the deceased's legal representative, and recovery will be limited to:
options: The property of the deceased that has come into the legal representative's hands
The legal representative's personal assets without limit
No recovery is possible after the judgment-debtor's death
mcqs.answer: The property of the deceased that has come into the legal representative's hands

mcqs.question: Two decree-holders, A and B, both hold money decrees against the same judgment-debtor and have applied for execution before the judgment-debtor's assets are realised by the court. When the assets are insufficient to satisfy both decrees fully, the assets are distributed between A and B:
options: Rateably, in proportion to the amounts of their respective decrees, under S.73
Entirely to whichever decree-holder applied first
Entirely to whichever decree is larger in amount
Entirely to the government, pending further litigation
mcqs.answer: Rateably, in proportion to the amounts of their respective decrees, under S.73

mcqs.question: A private citizen intends to sue the Government for compensation arising from an act done by a government officer in the discharge of his official duties. Before instituting the suit, the citizen must generally:
options: Serve a notice under S.80 at least two months before filing suit
File the suit directly without any notice
Obtain prior sanction from the Attorney General personally
Wait five years from the date the cause of action arose
mcqs.answer: Serve a notice under S.80 at least two months before filing suit

mcqs.question: A plaintiff has a single cause of action against a defendant entitling him to claim both possession of property and mesne profits, but he deliberately omits the claim for mesne profits in his suit for possession without seeking leave of the court. He later files a fresh suit for mesne profits alone. This second suit is most likely:
mcqs.answer: Barred under Order II Rule 2

mcqs.question: In a suit for eviction, a tenant could have raised, but did not raise, a specific defence of unlawful eviction procedure that was available and known to him at the time. After losing the suit, he files a fresh suit raising exactly that defence as a cause of action. This is most likely barred by:
options: Constructive res judicata under Explanation IV to S.11
Order II Rule 2 exclusively, and not S.11 at all
No bar applies, since it is a different suit
mcqs.answer: Constructive res judicata under Explanation IV to S.11

options: Refuse the injunction, as damages would be an adequate and efficacious remedy
Grant the injunction automatically, since any threatened harm justifies it
Grant the injunction only if the plaintiff pays extra court fees
Dismiss the suit altogether for want of a proper cause of action
mcqs.question: A plaintiff seeks a temporary injunction to prevent a defendant from selling ordinary commercial goods that are readily available in the market and easily valued in money terms, and for which monetary compensation would fully satisfy the plaintiff's loss. The court is likely to:
mcqs.answer: Refuse the injunction, as damages would be an adequate and efficacious remedy

mcqs.question: A plaintiff urgently applies for a temporary injunction, showing that if notice is given to the defendant before the hearing, the defendant is likely to immediately dispose of the disputed property, defeating the very purpose of the injunction. The court may, in this situation, appropriately:
options: Grant an ex-parte ad-interim injunction under Order XXXIX Rule 3, and later hear the defendant
Refuse to hear the application until the defendant is served and appears
Refer the matter for mediation before any order can be passed
mcqs.answer: Grant an ex-parte ad-interim injunction under Order XXXIX Rule 3, and later hear the defendant

mcqs.question: A trial court refuses to grant a temporary injunction sought by the plaintiff. Aggrieved, the plaintiff wishes to challenge this refusal. The appropriate remedy is:
options: An appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1 read with S.104
A review under Order XLVII, since no appeal lies from interlocutory orders
A reference under S.113, since only the High Court Division can decide injunction matters
A fresh suit challenging the refusal
mcqs.answer: An appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1 read with S.104

mcqs.question: A trial court passes an interlocutory order refusing to add a necessary party under Order I Rule 10, and this order is one for which the law does not provide any appeal. The aggrieved party's most appropriate remedy, if the order shows a jurisdictional error, is:
mcqs.answer: Revision under S.115

mcqs.question: A decree for possession is executed and the decree-holder takes possession of the property. On appeal, the decree is reversed and the appellate court holds the original defendant entitled to possession. The defendant may now apply for restoration of possession and any resulting benefits, under:
mcqs.answer: S.144 (restitution)

mcqs.question: A minor wishes to institute a suit to recover property. Since a minor cannot sue in his own right procedurally, the suit must be instituted in his name through a properly appointed:
options: Next friend, as provided under Order XXXII
Guardian ad litem acting as plaintiff in his own name instead of the minor
Advocate acting purely in his personal capacity
Court officer appointed by the government
mcqs.answer: Next friend, as provided under Order XXXII

mcqs.question: A person wishing to file a suit but unable to afford the requisite court fee applies to sue as an indigent person. The court, before granting permission, will examine whether he possesses sufficient means, excluding his necessary property and the subject-matter of the suit itself, and will also examine whether his allegations disclose a:
options: Contractual obligation on the defendant's part only
mcqs.answer: Cause of action

mcqs.question: A plaintiff discovers, midway through trial, that his plaint suffers from a formal defect (e.g., wrong description of property) that will likely cause the suit to fail on technical grounds, though his underlying claim is sound. His best procedural option is to apply to:
options: Withdraw the suit with liberty to file a fresh suit under Order XXIII Rule 1
Simply stop appearing at hearings and let the suit be dismissed for default
Immediately file a second, parallel suit while the first is pending
Apply for review under Order XLVII, since the suit has not yet been decided
mcqs.answer: Withdraw the suit with liberty to file a fresh suit under Order XXIII Rule 1

mcqs.question: During the pendency of a suit, both parties reach a settlement and wish the court to record it and pass a decree accordingly. For the court to act on this, the compromise must be:
options: In writing and signed by the parties, as required under Order XXIII Rule 3
Purely oral, since written compromises are not recognised
Approved by the government before being recorded
Filed as a fresh suit for specific performance of the compromise
mcqs.answer: In writing and signed by the parties, as required under Order XXIII Rule 3

mcqs.question: The sole plaintiff in a pending suit for recovery of a debt dies during the pendency of the suit, and the right to sue survives to his heirs. If no application to bring the legal representatives on record is made within the period prescribed by law, the suit will:
options: Continue automatically in the name of the deceased
Be transferred automatically to a different court
Be converted into a criminal complaint
mcqs.answer: Abate

mcqs.question: After a suit has abated due to failure to substitute legal representatives within time, the plaintiff's heir later applies to set aside the abatement, showing that the delay was due to circumstances beyond his control (e.g., being unaware of the death for valid reasons). The court may set aside the abatement on being satisfied of:
options: Sufficient cause under Order XXII Rule 9
No cause at all being required
Payment of enhanced court fees only
mcqs.answer: Sufficient cause under Order XXII Rule 9

mcqs.question: A defendant, ordered by the court to make discovery of documents relevant to the suit, refuses to comply without justification. As a consequence under Order XI Rule 21, the court may:
options: Strike out his defence, placing him in the same position as if he had not defended
Automatically decide the suit in his favour as a penalty against the plaintiff
Dismiss the suit for the plaintiff's failure to compel discovery earlier
Refer the matter to arbitration compulsorily
mcqs.answer: Strike out his defence, placing him in the same position as if he had not defended

mcqs.question: During the course of pleadings and correspondence, the defendant has clearly and unambiguously admitted certain facts that are sufficient, if true, to entitle the plaintiff to the relief sought. The plaintiff may apply to the court for:
options: Judgment on admissions under Order XII Rule 6, without waiting for the full trial
Rejection of the defendant's written statement under Order VIII Rule 5 exclusively
A commission under Order XXVI to verify the admissions
Nothing; admissions have no procedural consequence until final judgment
mcqs.answer: Judgment on admissions under Order XII Rule 6, without waiting for the full trial

mcqs.question: A mortgagor wishes to redeem mortgaged property by paying the outstanding mortgage debt to the mortgagee, who refuses to accept payment or return the title documents. The mortgagor's appropriate remedy is a suit for redemption under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXXIV Rule 7

mcqs.question: A creditor holds a dishonoured cheque (a negotiable instrument) and wishes to recover the amount quickly, without the defendant being entitled to defend as a matter of right. The appropriate suit procedure is under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXXVII (summary procedure)

mcqs.question: A decree-holder, entitled to possession of immovable property under a decree, attempts to take possession but is physically resisted by a stranger to the suit who claims an independent right in the property. The decree-holder's appropriate remedy is to make a complaint under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 97

mcqs.question: Property belonging to X (a third party, not the judgment-debtor) is mistakenly attached in execution of a decree against Y. X wishes to have the attachment lifted. His appropriate remedy is to file a claim/objection under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 58

mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor's immovable property is sold in execution, but he claims there was fraud in publishing the sale proclamation, resulting in a grossly inadequate price and substantial injury to him. His remedy is an application under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 90

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Deposit to Set Aside Sale
mcqs.question: A judgment-debtor, instead of alleging any irregularity in the sale, simply wishes to prevent confirmation of the sale of his property by paying the entire decretal amount, interest and costs into court before the sale is confirmed. His remedy lies under:
mcqs.answer: Order XXI Rule 89

mcqs.question: A first appellate court, in reversing the trial court's decree, has misapplied a settled principle of law in interpreting a contractual clause, and this affects the ultimate outcome. The losing party's remedy before the High Court Division is:
options: A second appeal under S.100, since a substantial question of law is involved
A fresh suit on the same cause of action
A revision under S.115 exclusively, and not a second appeal
An application for reference under S.113
mcqs.answer: A second appeal under S.100, since a substantial question of law is involved

mcqs.question: An appellant files an appeal challenging only part of a decree. The respondent, who is otherwise satisfied with the decree, later discovers a portion adverse to him that he also wishes to challenge, but he has not filed a separate appeal. Upon receiving notice of the appellant's appeal, the respondent may raise his objection by way of:
options: A review petition before the trial court
A revision petition, since cross-objections are not permitted under the CPC
mcqs.answer: Cross-objection under Order XLI Rule 22

mcqs.question: During the pendency of a first appeal, a party discovers crucial documentary evidence that was not available to him despite due diligence at the trial stage, and which is necessary for the appellate court to pronounce judgment. He may apply to the appellate court to:
options: Admit additional evidence under Order XLI Rule 27
Remand the entire case automatically to the trial court
File a fresh suit based on the newly discovered evidence
Seek review of the trial court's decree instead of pursuing the appeal
mcqs.answer: Admit additional evidence under Order XLI Rule 27

mcqs.question: After a decree is passed, a party discovers new and important evidence which, despite exercising due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time the decree was passed, and no appeal has yet been filed. His appropriate remedy before the same court is:
options: An application for review under Order XLVII Rule 1
A second appeal, since review is not available once a decree is passed
