A revision under S.115, since review is only for interlocutory orders
A fresh suit for the same relief, since review does not exist under the CPC
mcqs.answer: An application for review under Order XLVII Rule 1

mcqs.question: A subordinate court, while deciding a case, entertains a genuine and reasonable doubt as to whether a particular provision of a Regulation applies validly, and no appeal lies from its ultimate decree or order in the matter. The subordinate court may:
options: Refer the question for the opinion of the High Court Division under S.113 and Order XLVI
Decide the matter itself and never seek the High Court's opinion
Automatically stay the suit indefinitely pending clarification from the legislature
Dismiss the suit for want of jurisdiction
mcqs.answer: Refer the question for the opinion of the High Court Division under S.113 and Order XLVI

mcqs.question: A plaintiff obtains a decree for a specific sum of money as principal debt, and the contract between the parties provided for interest at a certain rate until payment. The court, in passing the decree, may additionally exercise discretion under S.34 to award:
options: Both pre-decree and post-decree (future) interest, as appropriate
Only pre-decree interest, since post-decree interest is never permitted
Only post-decree interest, since pre-decree interest is never permitted
No interest at all, since interest can only be claimed in a separate suit
mcqs.answer: Both pre-decree and post-decree (future) interest, as appropriate

mcqs.question: A defendant, in defending a suit, raises defences that are found by the court to be false and vexatious, causing the plaintiff unnecessary expense and delay. The plaintiff may seek compensatory costs from the defendant under:
options: S.35 alone, without any special provision
S.144, since it deals with restitution
O.XXV, since it deals with security for costs
mcqs.answer: S.35A

mcqs.question: A judgment passed by a court in a foreign country is sought to be enforced in Bangladesh, but it is shown that the foreign proceedings were conducted in a manner opposed to natural justice, and the defendant did not receive proper notice of the proceedings. Under S.13, such a judgment would most likely be considered:
options: Not conclusive, and therefore not enforceable in the ordinary manner
Automatically conclusive and binding, regardless of natural justice
Conclusive, but only binding on the plaintiff, not the defendant
Enforceable only after ratification by the government
mcqs.answer: Not conclusive, and therefore not enforceable in the ordinary manner

mcqs.question: A plaintiff has instituted a suit in a court which, though technically competent, is highly inconvenient for the defendant and most of the witnesses, who reside far away, and there is another competent court much closer to all concerned. The defendant may apply for transfer of the suit under:
options: S.22 (or S.24, depending on the level of court involved)
S.9, since it concerns jurisdiction over subject-matter
S.11, since it concerns res judicata
S.80, since it concerns notice requirements
mcqs.answer: S.22 (or S.24, depending on the level of court involved)

mcqs.question: A situation arises during trial for which no specific provision exists in the CPC, but the court finds it necessary to pass an order to prevent abuse of its process and secure the ends of justice. The court may invoke:
options: Only powers expressly enumerated, since inherent powers do not exist under the CPC
The government's discretion, by seeking prior approval
The Evidence Act exclusively, bypassing the CPC altogether
mcqs.answer: Its inherent powers under S.151

mcqs.question: After a decree is signed, it is discovered that a clerical mistake in the amount awarded (a simple addition error) needs correction, though the substance of the decision is unaffected. The proper procedure is to apply under:
options: S.152 for correction of clerical or arithmetical errors
Order XLVII for a full review of the merits
S.100 for a second appeal on this narrow point
O.IX R.13, treating it as an ex-parte decree issue
mcqs.answer: S.152 for correction of clerical or arithmetical errors

mcqs.question: A party fails to file a required document within the time fixed by the court due to circumstances beyond his control, and seeks additional time to comply. The court's general power to enlarge such time is found under:
options: S.149, which deals with payment of deficient court fees

mcqs.question: A plaint is found to be insufficiently stamped (i.e., inadequate court fee has been paid), but the deficiency appears to be a bona fide, curable error. S.149 empowers the court to allow the party to make good the deficiency of court fee, and where allowed, the document is treated as if the:
options: Proper fee had been paid from the beginning
Suit is treated as newly instituted from the date of payment, always
Suit is automatically dismissed regardless of the correction
Correction has no legal effect at all
mcqs.answer: Proper fee had been paid from the beginning

mcqs.question: A person apprehends that an application may soon be made against him in a pending or contemplated proceeding, without notice to him, and wishes to ensure the court hears him before passing any order. He may file a:
options: Written statement in advance under Order VIII
mcqs.answer: Caveat under S.148A

mcqs.question: Two individuals carrying on business in partnership wish to institute a suit against a debtor to recover money owed to their business. Instead of suing individually, they may institute the suit in the name of the:
options: Individual partners exclusively, since firms cannot sue
Managing partner alone, to the exclusion of the others
mcqs.answer: Firm, under Order XXX Rule 1

mcqs.question: A private limited company wishes to institute a suit against a supplier for breach of contract. The plaint may be signed and verified on behalf of the company by:
options: Its secretary, director, or other principal officer able to depose to the facts of the case
Only its Managing Director personally, and no one else
mcqs.answer: Its secretary, director, or other principal officer able to depose to the facts of the case

mcqs.question: A suit concerning breach of trust and mismanagement of a public charitable trust is contemplated by persons interested in the trust. Instead of individually suing, they wish to sue collectively for the benefit of the trust, and must, under the relevant provision, generally obtain:
options: The leave of the court, similar in structure to representative suits
Individual, separate suits without collective standing
Prior approval of the trustees themselves, defeating the purpose of the suit
Registration as a new legal entity before suing
mcqs.answer: The leave of the court, similar in structure to representative suits

mcqs.question: A public nuisance (e.g., unauthorized obstruction of a public road) affects a large number of persons in a locality. An individual affected member of the public wishes to bring a suit for a declaration and injunction in respect of this public nuisance. He must generally proceed with reference to:
options: S.91, which regulates suits in respect of public nuisances
S.92, which deals with public charitable trusts specifically
O.XXXV, which deals with interpleader suits
O.XXXIV, which deals with mortgage suits
mcqs.answer: S.91, which regulates suits in respect of public nuisances

mcqs.question: A suit falling within the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Court of Small Causes, and of a nature cognizable by such court, results in a decree adverse to the losing party, who wishes to appeal purely on a question of quantum of damages assessed (a question of fact, not law). Under S.96(4), such an appeal will most likely be:
options: Barred, since appeals from small cause decrees lie only on questions of law
Freely allowed on any ground, since S.96(4) has no restriction
Barred entirely, with no appeal or revision available under any law
Allowed only if the amount exceeds a very high threshold specified separately
mcqs.answer: Barred, since appeals from small cause decrees lie only on questions of law

mcqs.question: A plaintiff deliberately undervalues his claim to bring the suit within the pecuniary jurisdiction of a lower court, though the true value of the relief sought clearly exceeds that court's jurisdiction. If this comes to light, the appropriate consequence is most likely:
options: The court may require correction of valuation, and reject the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(b) if not corrected
The suit proceeds unaffected, since valuation is entirely at the plaintiff's discretion
The suit is automatically transferred to the High Court Division without any procedural step
The defendant is barred from raising any objection about valuation at any stage
mcqs.answer: The court may require correction of valuation, and reject the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(b) if not corrected

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Doctrine of Merger and Appeal
mcqs.question: A trial court's decree is appealed, and the appellate court, after hearing, confirms the decree in its entirety. For purposes of limitation in filing a further second appeal, the relevant date from which limitation begins to run is generally the date of the:
options: Appellate court's decree, due to the doctrine of merger
Original trial court's decree, since the appellate court merely confirmed it
Date the appeal was filed, regardless of when it was decided
Date the original suit was instituted
mcqs.answer: Appellate court's decree, due to the doctrine of merger

mcqs.question: In a pending suit, both issues of law (e.g., limitation, maintainability) and issues of fact arise, and the court believes that the suit may be disposed of entirely on the legal issues without going into evidence on facts. The court may, under Order XIV Rule 2, choose to:
options: Try the issues of law first, postponing the settlement of issues of fact
Necessarily try all issues together, since separate trial is never permitted
Refer the legal issue to the High Court Division mandatorily under S.113
Dismiss the suit outright without framing any issues at all
mcqs.answer: Try the issues of law first, postponing the settlement of issues of fact

mcqs.question: A decree-holder, having obtained a money decree, is unable to locate any attachable property of the judgment-debtor, and suspects the judgment-debtor has undisclosed assets. He may apply to the executing court to:
options: Examine the judgment-debtor as to his property and assets under Order XXI Rule 41
Immediately have the judgment-debtor arrested without any inquiry
File a fresh suit to discover the judgment-debtor's assets
Refer the matter to the police for investigation
mcqs.answer: Examine the judgment-debtor as to his property and assets under Order XXI Rule 41

mcqs.question: A decree-holder wishes to bid for and purchase the very property being sold in execution of his own decree. Under Order XXI Rule 72, he may do so only with:
options: No permission required at all, since decree-holders are automatically entitled to bid
The judgment-debtor's written consent only, and no court order
The permission of the opposing counsel
mcqs.answer: The permission of the court

mcqs.question: An execution sale of immovable property has taken place, and no application to set it aside has been filed by any party within the prescribed time. The next procedural step for the executing court is to:
options: Confirm the sale, making it absolute, under Order XXI Rule 92
Automatically cancel the sale for lack of any application
Refer the matter to the appellate court for confirmation
mcqs.answer: Confirm the sale, making it absolute, under Order XXI Rule 92

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Doctrine of Res Judicata & Different Capacities
mcqs.question: A person sued in his individual capacity in an earlier suit later brings a fresh suit in his capacity as a trustee of a trust, concerning the same subject matter. Since he is litigating under a materially different title/capacity, the plea of res judicata based on the earlier suit will most likely:
options: Fail, because the requirement of litigating under the same title is not satisfied
Succeed automatically, since the same individual is the party in both suits
Succeed only if the trust was created before the earlier suit
Be irrelevant, since res judicata never considers capacity
mcqs.answer: Fail, because the requirement of litigating under the same title is not satisfied

mcqs.question: During the course of a suit, a party repeatedly seeks unnecessary adjournments, causing significant delay without valid justification, prejudicing the other side and burdening the court's time. The court may, in addition to other measures, impose costs on that party under:
options: S.35A, which deals only with false or vexatious claims/defences
O.XXV, which deals with security for costs by plaintiffs residing abroad
mcqs.answer: S.35B

mcqs.question: A defendant, upon being served with summons, fails to file his written statement within the time fixed by the court under Order VIII Rule 1, and does not seek any extension. The most likely procedural consequence, subject to the court's discretion, is that the suit may proceed to be:
options: Heard, treating the defendant as not having filed a defence, though the extent of consequence depends on judicial discretion and applicable rules
Automatically dismissed for the plaintiff's failure to prompt the defendant
Automatically decreed in the defendant's favour
mcqs.answer: Heard, treating the defendant as not having filed a defence, though the extent of consequence depends on judicial discretion and applicable rules

mcqs.question: Order VIII Rule 10 addresses the situation where a party fails to present a written statement called for by the court within the time fixed, empowering the court to:
options: Pronounce judgment against that party, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit
Automatically dismiss the suit with no discretion
Refer the matter for compulsory arbitration
Impose imprisonment on the defaulting party
mcqs.answer: Pronounce judgment against that party, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Suit Dismissed for Default, Restoration
mcqs.question: A suit is dismissed under Order IX Rule 8 because the plaintiff failed to appear while the defendant appeared and did not admit the claim. The plaintiff later applies to have the dismissal set aside, showing sufficient cause for his non-appearance on that day. His application should be made under:
options: Order IX Rule 13, since it concerns the defendant
Order XLVII Rule 1, since it is a review
mcqs.answer: Order IX Rule 9

mcqs.question: On the day fixed for hearing, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appears before the court, despite due service of notice/summons on both. Under Order IX Rule 3, the likely consequence is that the court will:
options: Decree the suit in favour of the plaintiff by default
Refer the matter compulsorily to mediation
mcqs.answer: Dismiss the suit

mcqs.question: In a suit for specific performance of a contract of sale, a subsequent purchaser of the same property from the same vendor, whose rights may be affected by the outcome, seeks to be added as a party even though the original plaintiff and defendant do not object. Such a person is generally treated by courts as a:
options: Proper party, whose addition assists in completely adjudicating the controversy, even if not strictly necessary
Complete stranger who can never be added under any circumstances
Necessary party without whom the suit cannot proceed at all
mcqs.answer: Proper party, whose addition assists in completely adjudicating the controversy, even if not strictly necessary
mcqs.reference: O.I R.10(2) (conceptual, necessary vs proper party distinction)

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Doctrine of Election Between Remedies
mcqs.question: A decree-holder has a decree that could be satisfied either by attachment and sale of the judgment-debtor's immovable property or by attachment of the judgment-debtor's salary. He initially opts for attachment of salary and receives partial satisfaction over time, then later seeks to also attach the immovable property for the balance. This combined pursuit of remedies for the unsatisfied balance is generally:
options: Permissible, as a decree-holder is not confined to a single mode of execution and may use successive or combined modes until full satisfaction
Never permissible, since the decree-holder is bound by his first choice of remedy forever
Permissible only with the judgment-debtor's written consent
Barred by res judicata, since the mode of execution was earlier settled
mcqs.answer: Permissible, as a decree-holder is not confined to a single mode of execution and may use successive or combined modes until full satisfaction

mcqs.question: A private party seeks a temporary injunction against a government department restraining a specific administrative action pending disposal of the suit. Courts generally exercise:
options: Caution in granting injunctions against public authorities performing statutory functions, weighing public interest alongside the private party's case
No discretion at all, and must always grant such injunctions against the government
No discretion at all, and must always refuse such injunctions against the government
Discretion identical to private disputes, with no special consideration for public interest
mcqs.answer: Caution in granting injunctions against public authorities performing statutory functions, weighing public interest alongside the private party's case

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Void Decree and Collateral Attack
mcqs.question: A decree was passed by a court that, as a matter of law, entirely lacked subject-matter jurisdiction over the type of dispute involved (e.g., a matter exclusively reserved for a specialized tribunal). Years later, this decree is sought to be enforced. The judgment-debtor may challenge its validity:
options: Even in execution proceedings, or wherever it is sought to be relied upon, since it is a nullity
Only by filing a fresh appeal, since collateral attack on a decree is never permitted
Only within thirty days of the original decree, after which it becomes conclusively valid
Not at all, since decrees can never be challenged once passed
mcqs.answer: Even in execution proceedings, or wherever it is sought to be relied upon, since it is a nullity

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Multiple Defendants, Ex-parte Against One
mcqs.question: In a suit against two defendants, one appears and files a written statement, while the other, despite due service, does not appear. The court proceeds ex-parte against the non-appearing defendant while continuing the suit on contest against the appearing one. This is governed by principles under:
options: Order IX (appearance and consequences of non-appearance), applied separately to each defendant
Order XXII, since it concerns the death of parties
Order XXXII, since it concerns minors
Order XXXV, since it concerns interpleader
mcqs.answer: Order IX (appearance and consequences of non-appearance), applied separately to each defendant

mcqs.topic: Scenario - Suit for Injunction and Declaration Together
mcqs.question: A plaintiff seeks both a declaration of his title to property and a permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with his possession, both based on the same set of facts and filed in a single suit. This joinder of reliefs is generally:
options: Permissible, and does not violate the rule against splitting claims under Order II Rule 2, since it is a single cause of action with consequential relief
Impermissible, since only one relief may be sought per suit under the CPC
Permissible only with special leave of the High Court Division
Impermissible, since declaration and injunction cannot be combined under Bangladeshi procedural law
mcqs.answer: Permissible, and does not violate the rule against splitting claims under Order II Rule 2, since it is a single cause of action with consequential relief

mcqs.question: A plaintiff seeks to amend the plaint, after the expiry of limitation, merely to correct a clerical error in the description of the property already substantially identified in the original plaint, without altering the nature of the suit or introducing a new cause of action. Such an amendment is generally:
options: Allowed, since it does not introduce a new cause of action and merely clarifies the existing claim
Barred automatically, since any amendment after limitation is void
Allowed only with the defendant's written consent, regardless of the nature of the correction
Treated as tantamount to filing a fresh suit, subject to fresh limitation
mcqs.answer: Allowed, since it does not introduce a new cause of action and merely clarifies the existing claim

mcqs.question: A plaintiff wishes to obtain, before trial, sworn written answers from the defendant on specific factual matters relevant to the suit, believing this will narrow the issues and save time at trial. The appropriate procedural mechanism is to seek leave to deliver:
options: A notice to admit facts under Order XII Rule 4
A commission under Order XXVI Rule 9
An application for discovery of documents under Order XI Rule 12, exclusively
mcqs.answer: Interrogatories under Order XI Rule 1

mcqs.question: In a suit concerning a dispute over the exact boundaries of adjoining plots of land, the court finds it necessary to have an on-site inspection and technical measurement conducted by an expert to elucidate the matter in dispute. The court may issue a commission for this purpose under:
options: Order XXVI Rule 1 (examination of witnesses unable to attend)
Order XIII Rule 10 (inspection of documents in a public officer's possession)
mcqs.answer: Order XXVI Rule 9 (local investigation)

mcqs.question: Considering the overall scheme of the CPC 1908, a candidate preparing for the BJSC exam should note that the body of the Code (Sections 1-158) largely contains provisions of a general and relatively permanent character, while the First Schedule (Orders and Rules) deals mainly with matters of procedure and detail, and this structural division allows procedural rules to be amended more flexibly by:
options: High Court Division rule-making power under S.122, without requiring full legislative amendment for many procedural changes
The legislature exclusively, with no delegated rule-making power at all
The Executive branch exclusively, bypassing the judiciary entirely
No one; the First Schedule is as rigid as the body of the Code
mcqs.answer: High Court Division rule-making power under S.122, without requiring full legislative amendment for many procedural changes
